title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
嘉靖七年當大比士湖廣藩
司遵
著令馳使請主試官于禮部禮
部疏郎中臣日休主事臣龍
請于
朝
===
制曰可乃啓行於五月壬辰八月
壬寅戾止湖湘御史臣符司
監臨來會同考試官學正臣
大奇教諭臣屺臣鳳鳴臣縉
臣士載臣賢訓導臣愃臣本
純亦先後至臣等曰今日之
事
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

嘉靖七年，當大比士，湖廣藩司遵著令，馳使請主試官于禮部。禮部疏郎中臣日休、主事臣龍，請于朝。制曰：「可。」乃啓行於五月壬辰，八月壬寅戾止湖湘。御史臣符司監臨，來會。同考試官學正臣大奇、教諭臣屺、臣鳳鳴、臣縉、臣士載、臣賢，訓導臣愃、臣本純，亦先後至。臣等曰：「今日之事
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the seventh year of Jiajing [1528], when the triennial examination of scholars was due, the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission, following established regulations, dispatched an envoy with all speed to request chief examiners from the Ministry of Rites. The Ministry submitted a memorial nominating your servants Rixiu, a bureau director, and Long, a secretary, and requested the court’s approval. The Emperor’s decree reads: “Approved.” We then set out on the renchen day of the fifth month and arrived in Huxiang on the renyin day of the eighth month. Your servant Fu, an investigating censor serving as Supervising Official, came to meet us. The Associate Examiners—your servant Daqi, a department school instructor; your servants Qi, Fengming, Jin, Shizai, and Xian, county school instructors; and your servants Xuan and Benchun, assistant instructors—also arrived in succession. We, your servants, said: “The business before us today…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
君事也簾以内考試者主之簾以
外監臨者主之明試事貞憲
度求無負我
皇上求賢待士之意乃各慎攸司
試有提調以左布政使臣儀
左參政臣銳為之有監試以
按察使臣期雍僉事臣鉞為
===
之廼若鎮守太監臣潘真巡
撫右副都御史臣朱廷聲總
兵官清平伯臣吳傑皆祗承
明德無敢少懈右布政使臣胡訓
右參政臣徐金陵副使臣侯
綸臣胡岳臣張鯤左參議臣
許路右參議臣蔣同仁臣崔
punctuated:
君事也。簾以内，考試者主之；簾以外，監臨者主之。明試事，貞憲度，求無負我皇上求賢待士之意。」乃各慎攸司。
試有提調，以左布政使臣儀、左參政臣銳為之；有監試，以按察使臣期雍、僉事臣鉞為之。廼若鎮守太監臣潘真、巡撫右副都御史臣朱廷聲、總兵官清平伯臣吳傑，皆祗承明德，無敢少懈。右布政使臣胡訓、右參政臣徐金陵、副使臣侯綸、臣胡岳、臣張鯤、左參議臣許路、右參議臣蔣同仁、臣崔
translation_en:
…are the sovereign’s affairs. Within the curtain, the Examiners take charge; outside the curtain, the Supervising Official takes charge. We must conduct the examination with discernment and uphold the established regulations, seeking not to disappoint our Emperor’s intention to seek worthy men and treat scholars with due regard.” Each then conscientiously attended to his assigned duties.
The examination had Proctors: your servants Yi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Rui, Left Provincial Vice Administration Commissioner, served in this capacity. It also had examination monitors: your servants Qiyong, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Yue, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, served in this capacity. As for your servants Pan Zhen, the Regional Command Eunuch; Zhu Tingsheng, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; and Wu Jie, Regional Commander and Earl of Qingping, all reverently upheld the Emperor’s illustrious virtue, none daring to slacken in the least. Your servants Hu Xun, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Xu Jinling, Right Provincial Vice Administration Commissioner; Hou Lun, Hu Yue, and Zhang Kun, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Xu Lu, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Jiang Tongren, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; and Cui…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
桐僉事臣汪溱臣何鰲臣柴
經臣蔣珙咸綜理防範于外
其副使臣屠應塤右叅議臣
楊易先期入
賀戊申乃合提學副使臣許宗魯
所取士二千四百有竒棘院
試之辛亥又試之甲寅又試
===
之拔其尤者八十五人錄其
姓氏若文以
獻臣當序之首乃言曰我
太祖高皇帝設科最得古人取士
之意而得人之盛真可與古
相方其所以致雍熈悠久者
夫豈無自哉然或者謂以文
punctuated:
桐、僉事臣汪溱、臣何鰲、臣柴經、臣蔣珙，咸綜理防範于外。其副使臣屠應塤、右叅議臣楊易，先期入賀。戊申，乃合提學副使臣許宗魯所取士二千四百有竒，棘院試之。辛亥，又試之。甲寅，又試之。拔其尤者八十五人，錄其姓氏若文以獻。
臣當序之首，乃言曰：我太祖高皇帝設科，最得古人取士之意，而得人之盛，真可與古相方。其所以致雍熈悠久者，夫豈無自哉？然或者謂以文
translation_en:
…Tong, together with Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wang Zhen, He Ao, Chai Jing, and Jiang Gong, all oversaw arrangements and safeguards outside the examination compound. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Tu Yingxun and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Yang Yi had gone to court beforehand to offer congratulations. On the wushen day, the more than 2,400 candidates selected by Xu Zonglu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, were assembled and examined in the examination compound. On the xinhai day they were examined again, and on the jiayin day once more. Eighty-five of the most outstanding were selected, and their names and writings were recorded for presentation to the throne.
Your servant, charged with writing the opening preface, therefore says: Our Emperor Taizu Gao, in establishing the examinations, captured most fully the intent of the ancients in selecting men for office. The abundance of worthy men obtained could truly rival that of antiquity. Could the enduring harmony and prosperity thereby achieved possibly have been without a source? Yet some say that, by means of literary composition…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
取士非古也而得人則或猶
夫古焉夫得人猶古而曰取
士以文非古非也蓋古者敷
奏以言言心之聲也文乃言
之華者耳其爲心之聲均也
然今之文失古之聲也今之
制失古之意也官以試爲名
===
所以試士也人品或混於堂
下而考校反屬之他官文以
明道也習故者失之陳腐好
異者流之纖新程式有文所
以錄士之文以式也乃皆出
於主司之代筆客乘主也世
變日趨非我
punctuated: 取士非古也，而得人則或猶夫古焉。夫得人猶古，而曰取士以文非古，非也。蓋古者敷奏以言，言，心之聲也；文乃言之華者耳，其爲心之聲均也。然今之文失古之聲也，今之制失古之意也。官以試爲名，所以試士也；人品或混於堂下，而考校反屬之他官。文以明道也，習故者失之陳腐，好異者流之纖新。程式有文，所以錄士之文以式也；乃皆出於主司之代筆，客乘主也。世變日趨，非我
translation_en:
…selecting men through literary composition is not the ancient practice, yet the men thus obtained may still equal those of antiquity. But if the men obtained equal those of antiquity, it is wrong to say that selecting men through literary composition is not the ancient practice. In antiquity, men presented their accomplishments in words. Words are the voice of the heart; literary composition is merely the embellishment of words. In serving as the voice of the heart, they are the same.

Yet literary composition today has lost the voice of antiquity, and the institutions of today have lost the intent of antiquity. Officials bear the title of Examiner because their task is to examine candidates; yet men of disparate character may be mingled below the hall, while the assessment is instead entrusted to other officials. Literary composition serves to illuminate the Way; yet those who follow established practices fall into stale clichés, while those who delight in novelty lapse into finicky innovation. Model compositions are provided as standards: candidates’ compositions are recorded to serve as models. Yet these are all produced by ghostwriters for the presiding examiners—the guest usurps the host’s place. As the ways of the age change, they tend ever further in this direction, contrary to our …

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
高皇立法之初意故近者大臣建
議一曰正文體崇雅黜浮也
二曰明實錄文必于其人也
三曰慎考官主之者必以賢
也皆所以復
高祖之法之舊以賛我嘉靖之治
上可其奏乃下之禮部行自
===
國都外及藩省而
聖子
神孫可世守而勿失者也是舉也
孝廟之世亦嘗行之然祗承僅止
於兩省故事仍踵於他科文
體雖號為純正代筆猶屬之
主司未若
punctuated:
高皇立法之初意。故近者大臣建議：一曰正文體，崇雅黜浮也；二曰明實錄，文必于其人也；三曰慎考官，主之者必以賢也。皆所以復高祖之法之舊，以賛我嘉靖之治。上可其奏，乃下之禮部，行自國都，外及藩省，而聖子神孫可世守而勿失者也。
是舉也，孝廟之世亦嘗行之，然祗承僅止於兩省，故事仍踵於他科。文體雖號為純正，代筆猶屬之主司，未若
translation_en:
…the original intent of our founding Emperor Gao in establishing these regulations. Thus, recently, high ministers proposed: first, to rectify literary style by honoring elegance and rejecting superficiality; second, to ensure the authenticity of the recorded essays, so that each essay must be the work of the person to whom it is attributed; and third, to select Examiners carefully, ensuring that those presiding are worthy men. All these measures serve to restore the founding ancestor’s original regulations and assist the governance of our Jiajing reign. The emperor approved their memorial and referred it to the Ministry of Rites for implementation, beginning in the imperial capital and extending outward to the provinces, so that his sage sons and divine grandsons might uphold these regulations generation after generation without letting them lapse.
These measures had also been implemented during the reign of Emperor Xiaozong. Yet compliance extended to only two provinces, while other examination sessions continued to follow established precedent. Although the literary style was said to be pure and correct, the presiding Examiners still undertook the writing of substitute essays. This did not compare with…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
今日制之備行之廣垂之遠也
於乎休哉臣樗材被
命職司考校與諸士子相知以
文者知其文者冀知其心也
諸士之文其以心與其不以
心與皆未可知也其以心也
則亦已矣或不以心而徒夫
===
言已也其將何以稱
明詔而當
帝心與於乎諸士其毋徒夫言焉
爾矣
戶部山西清吏司郎中郭日休
謹序
punctuated:
今日制之備、行之廣、垂之遠也。於乎休哉！臣樗材，被命職司考校，與諸士子相知以文者，知其文者，冀知其心也。諸士之文，其以心與？其不以心與？皆未可知也。其以心也，則亦已矣；或不以心，而徒夫言已也，其將何以稱明詔而當帝心與？於乎！諸士其毋徒夫言焉爾矣！
戶部山西清吏司郎中郭日休謹序。
translation_en:
…the comprehensiveness of today’s regulations, the breadth of their implementation, and their enduring transmission to posterity. Ah, how splendid! Your servant, as worthless as the timber of an ailanthus tree, received the command to take charge of examining and assessing the candidates. My acquaintance with these scholars is through their writing; in knowing their writing, I hope to know their hearts. Whether their compositions come from the heart or do not come from the heart cannot yet be known. If they come from the heart, all is well. But if they do not, and amount merely to words, how will they accord with the enlightened edict and satisfy the Emperor’s heart? Ah, scholars, do not let these be mere words!
Preface respectfully written by Guo Rixiu, Director of the Shanxi Bureau in the Ministry of Revenue.

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:

巡按湖廣監察御史唐符〔信伯直隸常熟縣籍太倉州人甲戌進士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使盛儀〔德章直隸江都縣人乙丑進士〕

湖廣等處提刑按察司僉事陸鉞〔舉之浙江鄞縣人辛巳進士〕
===

禮部祠祭清吏司主事吳龍〔允際浙江孝豐縣人丙戌進士〕

山東萊州府平度州儒學學正陳大竒〔偉先福建莆田縣人己卯貢士〕
浙江處州府雲和縣儒學教諭汪𠆸〔秀之直隸祁門縣人丙子貢士〕
江西撫州府臨川縣儒學教諭林鳳鳴〔周祥廣東海康縣人甲子貢士〕
福建漳州府龍巖縣儒學教諭黃縉〔宗儀廣東澄海縣人己卯貢士〕
江西瑞州府新昌縣儒學教諭陳士載〔以文福建莆田縣人癸酉貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按湖廣監察御史唐符〔信伯，直隸常熟縣籍，太倉州人，甲戌進士〕。

提調官：
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使盛儀〔德章，直隸江都縣人，乙丑進士〕。
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左參政邵銳〔思抑，浙江仁和縣人，戊辰進士〕。

監試官：
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使周期雍〔汝和，江西寧州人，戊辰進士〕。
湖廣等處提刑按察司僉事陸鉞〔舉之，浙江鄞縣人，辛巳進士〕。

考試官：
戶部山西清吏司郎中郭日休〔德夫，福建莆田縣人，辛巳進士〕。
禮部祠祭清吏司主事吳龍〔允際，浙江孝豐縣人，丙戌進士〕。

同考試官：
山東萊州府平度州儒學學正陳大竒〔偉先，福建莆田縣人，己卯貢士〕。
浙江處州府雲和縣儒學教諭汪𠆸〔秀之，直隸祁門縣人，丙子貢士〕。
江西撫州府臨川縣儒學教諭林鳳鳴〔周祥，廣東海康縣人，甲子貢士〕。
福建漳州府龍巖縣儒學教諭黃縉〔宗儀，廣東澄海縣人，己卯貢士〕。
江西瑞州府新昌縣儒學教諭陳士載〔以文，福建莆田縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Huguang Provincial Examination, seventh year of Jiajing (1528).

Supervising Official:
Tang Fu, Regional Inspector for Huguang and Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Xinbo. He was registered in Changshu County, Zhili, and was a native of Taicang Subprefecture; he became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the jiaxu year.

Proctors:
Sheng Yi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Dezhang. A native of Jiangdu County, Zhili, he became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.
Shao Rui, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Siyi. A native of Renhe County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.

Examination Inspectors:
Zhou Qiyong, Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Ruhe. A native of Ningzhou, Jiangxi, he became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.
Lu Yue, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Juzhi. A native of Yin County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the xinsi year.

Examiners:
Guo Rixiu, Director of the Shanxi Bureau in the Ministry of Revenue, had the courtesy name Defu. A native of Putian County, Fujian, he became a metropolitan graduate in the xinsi year.
Wu Long, Secretary of the Bureau of Sacrifices in the Ministry of Rites, had the courtesy name Yunji. A native of Xiaofeng County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.

Associate Examiners:
Chen Daqi, School Instructor at the Confucian School of Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Weixian. A native of Putian County, Fujian, he became a tribute student (gongshi) in the jimao year.
Wang [given name 𠆸, reading uncertain], School Instructor at the Confucian School of Yunhe County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Xiuzhi. A native of Qimen County, Zhili, he became a tribute student in the bingzi year.
Lin Fengming, School Instructor at the Confucian School of Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Zhouxiang. A native of Haikang County, Guangdong, he became a tribute student in the jiazi year.
Huang Jin, School Instructor at the Confucian School of Longyan County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, had the courtesy name Zongyi. A native of Chenghai County, Guangdong [?], he became a tribute student in the jimao year.
Chen Shizai, School Instructor at the Confucian School of Xinchang County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Yiwen. A native of Putian County, Fujian, he became a tribute student in the guiyou year.

text:

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
無為而治者其舜也與
溥博淵泉而時出之
人性之善也猶水之就下也人無有不善
水無有不下
易
乾道變化各正性命保合大和乃利貞
損益盈虛與時偕行
===
是故剛柔相摩八卦相盪
天地設位聖人成能人謀鬼謀百姓與能
書
五月南巡守至于南岳如岱禮八月西巡
守至于西岳如初十有一月朔巡守至
于北岳如西禮歸格于藝祖用特五載
一巡守群后四朝敷奏以言明試以功
車服以庸
罔俾阿衡專美有商
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

無為而治者，其舜也與？

溥博淵泉，而時出之。

人性之善也，猶水之就下也。人無有不善，水無有不下。

易

乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。

損益盈虛，與時偕行。

是故剛柔相摩，八卦相盪。

天地設位，聖人成能；人謀鬼謀，百姓與能。

書

五月南巡守，至于南岳，如岱禮。八月西巡守，至于西岳，如初。十有一月朔巡守，至于北岳，如西禮。歸格于藝祖，用特。五載一巡守，群后四朝。敷奏以言，明試以功，車服以庸。

罔俾阿衡專美有商。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Was not Shun one who governed through nonaction?”

“Vast and all-embracing, deep as a flowing spring, he manifests these qualities at the appropriate times.”

“The goodness of human nature is like water’s tendency to flow downward. There is no person who is not good, just as there is no water that does not flow downward.”

Book of Changes (Yijing)

“The Way of Qian changes and transforms; each thing thereby receives its proper nature and allotted existence. Preserving and uniting in supreme harmony, it is thus beneficial to remain correct and firm.”

“Decrease and increase, fullness and emptiness, all proceed in step with the times.”

“Thus the firm and yielding rub against one another, and the eight trigrams stir one another.”

“Heaven and earth take their appointed positions, and the sage brings their capacities to completion. People deliberate, the spirits deliberate, and the common people participate in what can be accomplished.”

Book of Documents (Shujing)

“In the fifth month, he made a tour of inspection to the south, reaching the Southern Sacred Peak and performing the same rites as at Dai. In the eighth month, he made a tour of inspection to the west, reaching the Western Sacred Peak and proceeding as before. In the eleventh month, he made a tour of inspection to the north, reaching the Northern Sacred Peak and performing the same rites as in the west. Upon his return, he went to the temple of his accomplished ancestor and offered a single bull. Once every five years he made a tour of inspection, and the various lords attended court four times. They presented their reports in words, were clearly assessed by their achievements, and received carriages and robes according to their service.”

“Do not let Aheng [Yi Yin] alone enjoy the glory of service to the Shang.”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
王拜手稽首曰公不敢不敬天之休來相
宅其作周匹休公既定宅伻來來視予
卜休恒吉我二人共貞公其以予萬億
年敬天之休拜手稽首誨言
三后協心同底于道
詩
知子之來之雜佩以贈之
鶴鳴于九臯聲聞于野魚潜在淵或在于
渚樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維搉他山
===
之石可以為錯
釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣告于文人錫山土田
于周受命自召祖命虎拜稽首天子萬
年虎拜稽首對揚王休作召公考天子
萬壽明明天子令聞不已矢其文德洽
此四國
受小球大球為下國綴旒何天之休
春秋
無駭帥師入極〔隱公二年〕翬帥師〔隱公四〕
punctuated:
王拜手稽首曰：「公不敢不敬天之休，來相宅，其作周匹休。公既定宅，伻來，來視予卜，休恒吉。我二人共貞，公其以予萬億年敬天之休！」拜手稽首誨言。
三后協心，同底于道。
詩
知子之來之，雜佩以贈之。
鶴鳴于九臯，聲聞于野；魚潜在淵，或在于渚。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維搉。他山之石，可以為錯。
釐爾圭瓚，秬鬯一卣，告于文人。錫山土田，于周受命，自召祖命。虎拜稽首：「天子萬年！」虎拜稽首，對揚王休，作召公考：「天子萬壽！明明天子，令聞不已，矢其文德，洽此四國。」
受小球大球，為下國綴旒，何天之休。
春秋
無駭帥師入極〔隱公二年〕。翬帥師〔隱公四〕
translation_en:
The king bowed with his hands joined and his head to the ground, saying: “You, Duke, dared not fail to revere Heaven’s favor. You came to inspect the site of the capital, thereby bringing Zhou a matching blessing. Having determined the site, you sent a messenger to show me the divination: it was favorable and consistently auspicious. Let us two together uphold what is right. May you enable me, for countless years, to revere Heaven’s favor!” He bowed with his hands joined and his head to the ground in response to these words of instruction.
The three sovereigns united their hearts and together attained the Way.
Book of Odes
Knowing that you would come, I give you assorted girdle pendants.
The crane cries in the deep marshes; its voice is heard in the open country. Fish hide in the depths, or dwell by the islets. Pleasant is that garden, where sandalwood trees grow; beneath them are fallen leaves [?]. Stones from another mountain can serve as whetstones.
“I bestow on you a jade-handled libation ladle and a vessel of black-millet sacrificial wine, to announce this to your illustrious ancestors. I grant you mountains, lands, and fields. Receive your charge at Zhou, following the charge given to your ancestor of Shao.” Hu bowed with his head to the ground: “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!” Hu bowed with his head to the ground and gratefully extolled the king’s favor, accomplishing the work of the Duke of Shao: “May the Son of Heaven enjoy ten thousand years of life! The illustrious Son of Heaven’s good fame never ceases. He spreads his civil virtue throughout the states of the four quarters.”
He receives the small and large jade spheres, serves as the binding cord of the states below, and bears Heaven’s favor.
Spring and Autumn Annals
Wuhai led an army into Ji. 〔Second year of Duke Yin〕 Hui led an army … 〔Fourth [year] of Duke Yin〕

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
年公子友如陳莊公二十五年臧孫辰
告糴于齊莊公二十八年公子遂如齊
宣公元年季孫意如會晉荀躒于適歷
昭公三十一年
齊小白入于齊莊公九年
公孫歸父如晉宣公十八年叔弓帥師圍
費昭公十三年
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于
===
蕭魚襄公十一年
禮記
夫子之極言禮也可得而聞歟孔子曰我
欲觀夏道是故之杞而不足徵也吾得
夏時焉我欲觀殷道是故之宋而不足
徵也吾得坤乾焉
天道至教聖人至德
奮至德之光動四氣之和以著萬物之理
天子者與天地參故德配天地兼利萬物
punctuated:
年。公子友如陳，莊公二十五年。臧孫辰告糴于齊，莊公二十八年。公子遂如齊，宣公元年。季孫意如會晉荀躒于適歷，昭公三十一年。
齊小白入于齊，莊公九年。
公孫歸父如晉，宣公十八年。叔弓帥師圍費，昭公十三年。
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚，襄公十一年。
禮記
夫子之極言禮也，可得而聞歟？孔子曰：「我欲觀夏道，是故之杞，而不足徵也，吾得夏時焉。我欲觀殷道，是故之宋，而不足徵也，吾得坤乾焉。」
天道至教，聖人至德。
奮至德之光，動四氣之和，以著萬物之理。
天子者，與天地參，故德配天地，兼利萬物。
translation_en:
…year.
Prince You went to Chen. Twenty-fifth year of Duke Zhuang.
Zangsun Chen requested permission to purchase grain in Qi. Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang.
Prince Sui went to Qi. First year of Duke Xuan.
Jisun Yiru met Xun Li of Jin at Shili. Thirty-first year of Duke Zhao.

Xiaobai of Qi entered Qi. Ninth year of Duke Zhuang.

Gongsun Guifu went to Jin. Eighteenth year of Duke Xuan.
Shu Gong led an army to besiege Fei. Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu. Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.

Record of Rites (Liji)

“May we hear the Master’s fullest exposition of ritual?” Confucius said: “I wished to examine the Way of Xia, and therefore went to Qi, but there was insufficient evidence to substantiate it. I obtained the Seasons of Xia there. I wished to examine the Way of Yin, and therefore went to Song, but there was insufficient evidence to substantiate it. I obtained the Kun-Qian there.”

The Way of Heaven is the highest teaching; the sage embodies the highest virtue.

He brings forth the radiance of the highest virtue and sets in motion the harmony of the energies of the four seasons, thereby making manifest the principles of all things.

The Son of Heaven forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. Thus his virtue matches Heaven and Earth, and he benefits all things…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
與日月並明明照四海而不遺微小
第貳塲
論
君子之道費而隱
詔誥表內科壹道
擬漢除挾書律詔惠帝二年
擬唐以楊綰為中書侍郎同平章事誥大
曆十二年
擬宋以翰林學士歐陽脩知貢舉謝表嘉
===
祐二年
判語五條
舉用有過官吏
檢踏災傷田糧
術士妄言禍福
縱放軍人歇役
詐欺官私取財
第叁塲
策五道
punctuated:
與日月並明，明照四海而不遺微小。

第貳塲。
論：君子之道費而隱。
詔誥表內科壹道。
擬漢除挾書律詔，惠帝二年。
擬唐以楊綰為中書侍郎、同平章事誥，大曆十二年。
擬宋以翰林學士歐陽脩知貢舉謝表，嘉祐二年。
判語五條：舉用有過官吏；檢踏災傷田糧；術士妄言禍福；縱放軍人歇役；詐欺官私取財。

第叁塲。
策五道。
translation_en:
…shines alongside the sun and moon, illuminating all within the four seas without overlooking even the smallest things.

Second Session
Discourse: “The Way of the gentleman is far-reaching yet hidden.”
One composition from among the edict, proclamation, and memorial categories [?].
Draft an edict abolishing the law against possessing books under the Han, dated the second year of Emperor Hui’s reign.
Draft a proclamation appointing Yang Wan as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Joint Manager of Affairs under the Tang, dated the twelfth year of Dali.
Draft a memorial of thanks by the Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xiu upon being appointed to administer the civil-service examination under the Song, dated the second year of Jiayou.
Five legal judgments: recommending and employing officials and clerks with prior offenses; inspecting farmland damaged by disasters and its grain-tax assessments; diviners making unfounded pronouncements about misfortune and good fortune; allowing soldiers to leave their duties; obtaining government or private property by fraud.

Third Session
Five policy questions.

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
問創業垂統之君與中興之主皆有謨訓
以遺後世若典謨訓誥諸書純乎無以
議也下至漢唐宋之英君誼辟其所遺
一代之典章亦有符於古否乎我
太祖高皇帝首創洪基今
聖天子入繼大統其
聖謨嘉言見於史氏之所書儒臣之所記嘗竊
窺其一二莫不盡善盡美真與典謨訓
誥相爲表裏然
===
高皇
聖上非徒言之亦允蹈之見於脩齊治平以爲
創業中興之懿其必有可言者諸士子
請揚厲之以鳴
國家之盛
問三禮之書聖人治天下之大經大法也
慨自脱落於去籍之後掇拾於煨燼之
餘周禮六典而缺冬官論者謂冬官之
不缺儀記二禮各自爲書論者謂經傳
punctuated:
問：創業垂統之君與中興之主，皆有謨訓以遺後世。若典謨訓誥諸書，純乎無以議也。下至漢唐宋之英君誼辟，其所遺一代之典章，亦有符於古否乎？我太祖高皇帝首創洪基，今聖天子入繼大統，其聖謨嘉言，見於史氏之所書、儒臣之所記。嘗竊窺其一二，莫不盡善盡美，真與典謨訓誥相爲表裏。然高皇、聖上非徒言之，亦允蹈之，見於脩齊治平，以爲創業中興之懿，其必有可言者。諸士子請揚厲之，以鳴國家之盛。

問：三禮之書，聖人治天下之大經大法也。慨自脱落於去籍之後，掇拾於煨燼之餘，周禮六典而缺冬官，論者謂冬官之不缺；儀記二禮各自爲書，論者謂經傳
translation_en:
Question: Rulers who founded dynasties and established lines of succession, and sovereigns who restored dynastic fortunes, all left counsels and instructions to posterity. Such writings as the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements are pure and beyond reproach. Coming down to the illustrious rulers and worthy sovereigns of the Han, Tang, and Song, did the institutions and regulations they bequeathed to their respective dynasties likewise accord with antiquity? Our Emperor Taizu Gao first laid the great foundations, and now our sagely Son of Heaven has succeeded to the imperial line. Their sagely counsels and excellent sayings appear in the writings of historians and the records of Confucian officials. Having ventured to examine a few of these, we find them wholly good and wholly beautiful, truly complementing the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements. Yet Emperor Gao and His Majesty have not merely spoken these words: they have faithfully put them into practice. Manifested in cultivating the self, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world, these constitute the admirable achievements of dynastic founding and restoration. There must surely be much to say about them. You candidates are invited to extol these achievements and thus proclaim the flourishing grandeur of our state.

Question: The books of the Three Rites embody the great guiding principles and laws by which the sages governed the world. Alas, after suffering losses through the removal of books [?], they were pieced together from what remained among the ashes. Of the six administrative divisions in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), the Winter Offices are missing, yet some commentators maintain that the Winter Offices are not missing. The Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) and the Records of Rites (Liji) each constitute a separate book, yet some commentators maintain that the classic and its commentary …

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之相附吳文正公奮乎百世之下作為
三禮考註取他官以補冬官之缺尊儀
禮以為禮記之經考之前言而孰據質
之文義而何居且置官之意尚有可疑
而篇目增損不能無憾請詳言之以觀
考古之學
問六經之道同歸而禮樂之用為急禮樂
之制既亡而樂之壞尤甚請以所聞一
二與諸子商之功成作樂夫古有初六
===
經何者為論樂之始律呂既亡歷世無
考六樂何以得創作之妙十二律一也
黄鍾何以為重五音一也宫何以為主
八音之序何先於金石二音之變何獨
於宫徴擅神解之名得暗解之譽何以
無補於樂以鍾律為本以秬黍為則何
以不得其平若周濂溪程伊川張横渠
蔡西山四子皆有復古樂之論舉而行
之果可以復制作之妙否與請試陳之
punctuated:
之相附。吳文正公奮乎百世之下，作為《三禮考註》，取他官以補冬官之缺，尊《儀禮》以為《禮記》之經。考之前言而孰據？質之文義而何居？且置官之意尚有可疑，而篇目增損不能無憾。請詳言之，以觀考古之學。
問：六經之道同歸，而禮樂之用為急。禮樂之制既亡，而樂之壞尤甚。請以所聞一二與諸子商之。功成作樂，夫古有初，六經何者為論樂之始？律呂既亡，歷世無考，六樂何以得創作之妙？十二律一也，黄鍾何以為重？五音一也，宫何以為主？八音之序，何先於金石？二音之變，何獨於宫徴？擅神解之名，得暗解之譽，何以無補於樂？以鍾律為本，以秬黍為則，何以不得其平？若周濂溪、程伊川、張横渠、蔡西山四子，皆有復古樂之論，舉而行之，果可以復制作之妙否與？請試陳之。
translation_en:
…that they are attached to one another as classic and commentary. Lord Wu Wenzheng, rising to the task a hundred generations later, composed Examination and Annotation of the Three Ritual Classics (Sanli kaozhu). He drew on the other offices to fill the missing Offices of Winter and elevated the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) to the status of the classic underlying the Record of Rites (Liji). When his work is examined against earlier statements, which provide its basis? When tested against the wording and meaning of the texts, how does it stand? Moreover, his understanding of the intention behind the establishment of offices remains open to question, and his additions and deletions of chapters cannot be without shortcomings. Please discuss this fully, so that we may assess your learning in the study of antiquity.
Question: The Way of the Six Classics leads to the same end, but the application of ritual and music is especially urgent. The institutions of ritual and music have already disappeared, and the deterioration of music is particularly severe. Let me offer one or two things I have heard for discussion with you candidates. Music is created when achievements have been accomplished; in antiquity there was a beginning [?]. Which of the Six Classics first discusses music? Since the pitch standards have disappeared and cannot be verified through the successive ages, how can the subtle art of creating the Six Musical Performances be recovered? The twelve pitches belong to one system: why is Huangzhong given particular importance? The five notes belong to one system: why is gong their principal note? In the ordering of the eight classes of instruments, why do metal and stone come first? Why are altered notes confined to gong and zhi? Why did those renowned for inspired understanding and praised for intuitive comprehension contribute nothing to music? With bell pitches as the foundation and black millet grains as the standard, why could proper tuning not be attained? The four masters Zhou Lianxi, Cheng Yichuan, Zhang Hengqu, and Cai Xishan all discussed restoring ancient music. If their proposals were put into practice, could the subtle art of its institution and creation truly be recovered? Please attempt to explain.

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
問刑者聖人愛民之具所以弼教而使之
弗入于邪也其見於典謨訓誥之書大
易記禮之言詳矣然論者或主於寬或
主於嚴而程子不取刻核之論朱子獨
憫夫死者之無辜其何所取中與大舜
之制刑文王之慎罰漢唐宋皆有刑法
志之作其寬乎其嚴乎張子謂治獄不
得其平者蓋有數說真西山帥長沙誡
同官六事將謂失於寬乎失於嚴乎自
===
漢以來司刑者有善可爲法惡可爲戒
見於
爲善陰隲歷代臣鑑之書者公私之辨寬嚴
之效如在目前諸子其明以告我
問識時務者在俊傑今日之務莫急於財
用而諸士有俊傑者敢以理財之道詢
焉三代之制莫備於成周而成周之制
莫詳於周禮繫之以九兩任之以九職
而又有九府九式之法卒至民殷國富
punctuated:
問：刑者，聖人愛民之具，所以弼教而使之弗入于邪也。其見於典謨訓誥之書、大易記禮之言詳矣。然論者或主於寬，或主於嚴，而程子不取刻核之論，朱子獨憫夫死者之無辜，其何所取中與？大舜之制刑，文王之慎罰，漢唐宋皆有刑法志之作，其寬乎？其嚴乎？張子謂治獄不得其平者，蓋有數說。真西山帥長沙，誡同官六事，將謂失於寬乎？失於嚴乎？自漢以來，司刑者有善可爲法、惡可爲戒，見於《爲善陰隲》《歷代臣鑑》之書者，公私之辨、寬嚴之效，如在目前。諸子其明以告我。

問：識時務者在俊傑。今日之務，莫急於財用，而諸士有俊傑者，敢以理財之道詢焉。三代之制，莫備於成周；而成周之制，莫詳於《周禮》。繫之以九兩，任之以九職，而又有九府九式之法，卒至民殷國富。
translation_en:
Question: Punishments are the means by which the sages express their love for the people, supplementing moral instruction and keeping them from straying into evil. This is set forth in detail in the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of the Book of Documents, and in the words of the great Book of Changes and the Record of Rites. Yet some commentators favor leniency, while others favor severity. Master Cheng rejected arguments for harsh scrutiny, and Master Zhu was particularly troubled by the innocence of those put to death. Where, then, should the proper mean be sought? Consider the penal institutions of the great Shun and King Wen’s caution in punishment. The histories of the Han, Tang, and Song all contain treatises on penal law: did these favor leniency or severity? Master Zhang offered several explanations for failures to achieve fairness in adjudicating cases. When Zhen Xishan held command at Changsha, he admonished his fellow officials on six matters. Were the failings he addressed ones of excessive leniency or excessive severity? Since the Han, officials administering punishments have displayed goodness worthy of emulation and wickedness that should serve as a warning, as recorded in Doing Good and Receiving Hidden Blessings (Weishan yinzhi) and A Mirror of Ministers through the Dynasties (Lidai chen jian). The distinction between public duty and private interest, and the effects of leniency and severity, appear as if before our very eyes. Let you gentlemen explain these matters clearly to me.

Question: Those who understand the pressing affairs of their times are men of outstanding talent. Among today’s concerns, none is more urgent than public finance. Since there are men of outstanding talent among you gentlemen, I venture to inquire into the proper way to manage it. Among the institutions of the Three Dynasties, none were more complete than those of the Zhou; and no account of Zhou institutions is more detailed than the Rites of Zhou. The people were bound together through the nine bonds and assigned responsibilities through the nine occupations. There were also regulations for the nine treasuries and the nine standards of expenditure. Ultimately, the people became prosperous and the state wealthy…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
則周禮信乎周公致太平之典也夫何
西漢之末熈寧元豐之間有用之者乃
至禍天下而亂國家耶漢至文帝唐至
太宗宋至祥符天禧之間可謂足於財
矣後世皆不免於財乏者其故何與昔
人謂天地間財只有此數不在官則在
民今日則官民俱困抑又何與此司
國計者不能無憂也其詳著于篇將轉以聞
于
===
上
punctuated: 則《周禮》信乎周公致太平之典也。夫何西漢之末、熈寧元豐之間，有用之者，乃至禍天下而亂國家耶？漢至文帝，唐至太宗，宋至祥符天禧之間，可謂足於財矣。後世皆不免於財乏者，其故何與？昔人謂：「天地間財只有此數，不在官則在民。」今日則官民俱困，抑又何與？此司國計者不能無憂也。其詳著于篇，將轉以聞于上。
translation_en: …then the Rites of Zhou is indeed the canon by which the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace. Why, then, did those who applied it at the end of the Western Han and during the Xining and Yuanfeng reign periods bring calamity upon all under Heaven and disorder to the state? Under Emperor Wen of the Han, Emperor Taizong of the Tang, and during the Xiangfu and Tianxi reign periods of the Song, financial resources could be called ample. Yet subsequent generations invariably suffered financial shortages. What was the reason? People of old said: “There is only this much wealth between Heaven and Earth; if it is not held by the government, it is held by the people.” Today, however, both government and people are in straitened circumstances. Why should this be? Those responsible for the state's finances cannot but be troubled by this. Set out your explanations fully in your essays, so that they may be forwarded for the Emperor's hearing.

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
無爲而治者其舜也與
周采
同考試官訓導余批帝舜神化人所難言
是作渾融爾雅若足以發其蘊錄之
同考試官教諭周批題有明註塲中士子
各主偏見殊戾無爲本㫖此作得之
考試官主事吳批明暢
===
考試官郎中郭批瑩潔無疵
聖人舉天下之至治歸諸有虞之至聖蓋治固
難而治至於無爲則尤難也求其可以當此者
舎舜奚以哉昔夫子意謂至人無爲大聖不作
吾甞於古而有徴矣彼君以化民爲難有爲而
後化則其治也勞矣治以民化爲極無爲而自
成則其於化也神矣是非不欲爲也惟玄惟默
而世巳底於隆平雖欲爲之將安施乎是非不
能爲也不識不知而民巳臻於康乂雖能爲之
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「無爲而治者，其舜也與？」
周采

同考試官訓導余批：帝舜神化，人所難言。是作渾融爾雅，若足以發其蘊，錄之。
同考試官教諭周批：題有明註，塲中士子各主偏見，殊戾無爲本㫖。此作得之。
考試官主事吳批：明暢。
考試官郎中郭批：瑩潔無疵。

聖人舉天下之至治，歸諸有虞之至聖。蓋治固難，而治至於無爲則尤難也。求其可以當此者，舎舜奚以哉？昔夫子意謂：至人無爲，大聖不作，吾甞於古而有徴矣。彼君以化民爲難，有爲而後化，則其治也勞矣；治以民化爲極，無爲而自成，則其於化也神矣。是非不欲爲也，惟玄惟默，而世巳底於隆平，雖欲爲之，將安施乎？是非不能爲也，不識不知，而民巳臻於康乂，雖能爲之
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Was Shun not the one who governed through nonaction?”
Zhou Cai

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: Emperor Shun’s wondrous transforming influence is difficult for people to express. This composition is thoroughly integrated, refined, and correct; it seems adequate to reveal the subject’s inner meaning. I select it for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: The topic has a clear commentary, yet the candidates in the examination each adhere to a partial view, gravely at odds with the fundamental meaning of nonaction. This composition grasps it.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Secretary: Clear and fluent.

Comment by Examiner Guo, Director: Lustrous and pure, without blemish.

The Sage attributed the most perfect government under Heaven to the supreme sage of Youyu, Shun. Governing is certainly difficult; to govern through nonaction is harder still. If we seek someone worthy of this description, whom could we choose but Shun? Formerly, the Master’s meaning was this: The perfected person acts without action; the great sage undertakes no contrived activity. I have found evidence of this in antiquity. Rulers regard transforming the people as difficult. If transformation comes only after deliberate action, their government is laborious. Government takes the transformation of the people as its highest attainment. If this comes about of itself, without action, then its transforming influence is wondrous indeed. This does not mean that he had no desire to act. Remaining profound and silent, he had already brought the age to flourishing peace. Even if he wished to act, where could he apply his efforts? This does not mean that he was incapable of acting. Without conscious knowing or awareness, the people had already attained well-being and good order. Even if he were capable of acting…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
將焉用與然若此者誰足以當之彼前此而帝
固非有為而後治也然不若舜之尤泯其迹焉
後此而王固皆無為而成化也然未若舜之尤
享其盛焉蓋其濬哲文明之德有以秘神化於
無形又况勞於前者有允恭克讓之聖事之可
為者而堯已為之則禮樂教化之洽自仰成於
重華之朝矣温恭允塞之德有以斡元功於莫
測又况勞於下者有禹臯稷契之賢事之可任
者而臣皆任之則雍熙悠乂之盛自不勞乎宵
===
旰之憂矣此舜之治所以度越帝王而超出百
代與抑夫子此言則舜若無所事事者然考之
書察器觀象輯瑞時巡封山濬川命官咨牧史
不絕筆則舜又若此之勤勞也嗚呼不讀魯論
無以知舜之逸不讀舜典無以知舜之勤合二
書觀之則聖人從事可見矣
溥博淵泉而時出之
胡彦
同考試官教諭陳 批 聖德淵微此題該括
punctuated:
將焉用與？然若此者，誰足以當之？彼前此而帝，固非有為而後治也，然不若舜之尤泯其迹焉；後此而王，固皆無為而成化也，然未若舜之尤享其盛焉。蓋其濬哲文明之德，有以秘神化於無形；又况勞於前者，有允恭克讓之聖，事之可為者，而堯已為之，則禮樂教化之洽，自仰成於重華之朝矣。温恭允塞之德，有以斡元功於莫測；又况勞於下者，有禹臯稷契之賢，事之可任者，而臣皆任之，則雍熙悠乂之盛，自不勞乎宵旰之憂矣。此舜之治所以度越帝王而超出百代與？抑夫子此言，則舜若無所事事者，然考之《書》，察器觀象，輯瑞時巡，封山濬川，命官咨牧，史不絕筆，則舜又若此之勤勞也。嗚呼！不讀《魯論》，無以知舜之逸；不讀《舜典》，無以知舜之勤。合二書觀之，則聖人從事可見矣。
溥博淵泉而時出之
胡彦
同考試官教諭陳批：聖德淵微，此題該括
translation_en:
…what use would there be for it? Yet who could truly merit such a description? Those who ruled as emperors before him certainly did not attain order only through deliberate action, but none effaced the traces of their actions as completely as Shun. Those who ruled as kings after him certainly all accomplished moral transformation through nonaction, but none enjoyed its full flourishing as Shun did. His profound wisdom and brilliant virtue enabled him to conceal his wondrous transforming influence within the formless. Moreover, the sage who had labored before him was truly reverent and capable of yielding: Yao had already done all that could be done. Thus the pervasive influence of rites, music, instruction, and moral transformation naturally came to fruition at the court of Chonghua—that is, Shun. His gentle, reverent, and truly sincere virtue enabled him to direct the great work of creation in unfathomable ways. Moreover, those who labored beneath him included such worthies as Yu, Gao Yao, Ji, and Xie. His ministers assumed every responsibility that could be entrusted to them, so the flourishing harmony and enduring peace of his reign naturally required no anxious toil from before dawn until late at night. Is this not why Shun’s government surpassed that of emperors and kings and rose above a hundred generations?
Yet these words of the Master make Shun appear to have had nothing whatever to do. If we examine the Book of Documents, however, we find him inspecting instruments and observing celestial phenomena, collecting jade tokens of investiture and making tours of inspection at the appointed times, establishing boundaries at mountains and dredging waterways, appointing officials and consulting regional governors. The historians’ brushes never ceased recording his deeds: Shun was also this diligent in his labors. Alas! Without reading the Lu Analects, one cannot know Shun’s ease; without reading the Canon of Shun, one cannot know his diligence. Read the two texts together, and the sage’s way of conducting affairs becomes apparent.
“Vast and far-reaching, deep as a spring, and issuing forth at the proper times”
Hu Yan
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The sage’s virtue is profound and subtle; this topic encompasses…”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
殆盡作者類弗能文之此篇認理真命詞當其
善於形容者乎
同考試官學正陳批作此題者類逞浮詞
殊非本色說理精當僅見此耳
考試官主事吳批說時出處迥異衆作
考試官郎中郭批語意渾融當是作者
中庸論聖德充積之盛而時見於外焉蓋積中
形外乃德盛自致也非天下之至聖孰能與於
此中庸承上章而言小德川流以發明天道意
===
謂惟天下之至聖聰明睿智既妙于生知仁義
禮智獨全其固有故其充積于中也太極之體
以全冒天下之道而無外天命之性以具統天
下之善而無餘充周不窮而無所限量其周遍
廣闊矣乎寂然不動而至靜之體足以立天下
之有退藏於密而於穆之妙有以具萬化之原
測之愈遠而資之益深其靜深有本矣乎所謂
充積於中者蓋如此然又感之遂通而全體呈
露不待見之而後章觸之即應而妙用顯行不
punctuated:
殆盡。作者類弗能文之，此篇認理真，命詞當，其善於形容者乎！
同考試官學正陳批：作此題者類逞浮詞，殊非本色。說理精當，僅見此耳。
考試官主事吳批：說時出處，迥異衆作。
考試官郎中郭批：語意渾融，當是作者。
《中庸》論聖德充積之盛，而時見於外焉。蓋積中形外，乃德盛自致也。非天下之至聖，孰能與於此？《中庸》承上章而言小德川流，以發明天道。意謂惟天下之至聖，聰明睿智既妙于生知，仁義禮智獨全其固有。故其充積于中也，太極之體以全，冒天下之道而無外；天命之性以具，統天下之善而無餘。充周不窮，而無所限量，其周遍廣闊矣乎！寂然不動，而至靜之體足以立天下之有；退藏於密，而於穆之妙有以具萬化之原。測之愈遠，而資之益深，其靜深有本矣乎！所謂充積於中者，蓋如此。然又感之遂通，而全體呈露，不待見之而後章；觸之即應，而妙用顯行，不
translation_en:
…almost entirely. Those who write on this topic generally fail to give it adequate literary expression. This essay grasps the principle truly and chooses its words aptly: surely it excels at portraying it!
Associate Examiner Chen, School Director, comments: Writers on this topic generally indulge in empty rhetoric, quite departing from its true character. For precise and fitting exposition of principle, I have seen only this essay.
Examiner Wu, Secretary, comments: Its explanation of “manifesting at the proper times” stands far apart from all the other essays.
Examiner Guo, Director, comments: Its language and meaning form a seamless whole. This is surely the work of an accomplished writer.
The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the abundant fullness of sagely virtue and its manifestation outwardly at the proper times. For inward accumulation taking outward form is the natural result of virtue’s abundance. Who but the utmost sage under Heaven could attain this? Following the preceding chapter, the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of lesser virtues flowing like rivers, elucidating the Way of Heaven. Its meaning is that only the utmost sage under Heaven possesses perception, understanding, discernment, and wisdom whose subtle excellence comes through innate knowledge, and preserves in their entirety his inherent benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. Thus, as these accumulate within him, the substance of the Supreme Ultimate is complete, encompassing all the ways under Heaven with nothing outside it; the nature conferred by Heaven is fully present, embracing all goodness under Heaven with nothing left over. All-pervading and inexhaustible, it admits no bounds or measure. How comprehensive and vast it is! Still and unmoving, its utterly tranquil substance suffices to establish all that exists under Heaven; withdrawing into hiddenness, its profound and unceasing subtlety contains the source of all transformations. The more one fathoms it, the farther it extends; the more one draws upon it, the deeper it grows. How tranquil, deep, and firmly rooted it is! Such is what is meant by accumulation within. Yet, when stimulated, it immediately penetrates all things, and its whole substance stands revealed: it does not await being seen before becoming manifest. Upon contact it responds at once, and its wondrous functioning becomes evident in action; it does not…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
待擬之而後合聰明睿智之德出焉則視遠聽
聰知來藏往而圓神不滯得夫時措之宜矣仁
義禮智之德出焉則以容以執以敬以别而旁
行不流效夫天下之動矣所謂時見於外者蓋
如此是則積于中者藏諸用也見於外者顯諸
仁也體用一原聖德之妙一至此哉抑此以充
積發見者而言非其極也故下文又言其積中
發外之盛而極夫配天之功必如是而後爲聖
德之全體聖學之極功也然則聖可學乎亦曰
===
先明諸心知所往而後力行以求至焉
人性之善也猶水之就下也人無有不善
水無有不下
曠宗舜
同考試官訓導郭 批 性善無不善處提掇
明白深得孟子悟時之意而繳尤見體認可與
言性矣
同考試官教諭林 批 理到之文自不費詞
可以式矣
punctuated:
待擬之而後合。聰明睿智之德出焉，則視遠聽聰，知來藏往，而圓神不滯，得夫時措之宜矣。仁義禮智之德出焉，則以容、以執、以敬、以别，而旁行不流，效夫天下之動矣。所謂時見於外者，蓋如此。是則積于中者，藏諸用也；見於外者，顯諸仁也。體用一原，聖德之妙一至此哉！抑此以充積發見者而言，非其極也。故下文又言其積中發外之盛，而極夫配天之功。必如是而後爲聖德之全體、聖學之極功也。然則聖可學乎？亦曰：先明諸心，知所往，而後力行以求至焉。

人性之善也，猶水之就下也。人無有不善，水無有不下。
曠宗舜

同考試官訓導郭批：性善無不善處，提掇明白，深得孟子悟時之意，而繳尤見體認，可與言性矣。

同考試官教諭林批：理到之文，自不費詞，可以式矣。
translation_en:
…without waiting for deliberation before attaining accord. When the virtues of clear perception and sagacious wisdom emerge, one sees far and hears acutely, knows what is to come and retains what has passed. Spiritually responsive in all directions and unobstructed, one attains what is appropriate in acting as circumstances require. When the virtues of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom emerge, one embraces, holds firm, shows reverence, and distinguishes; extending one's activity in all directions without being swept astray, one responds to the movements of all under Heaven. Such is what is meant by manifesting outwardly at the proper times. Thus, what accumulates within is concealed in its functioning; what appears outwardly is manifest in benevolence. Substance and function have a single source: how consummate is the subtlety of sagely virtue! Yet this speaks only of inward fullness and accumulation and their outward manifestation; it does not describe their ultimate extent. Hence the passage below further speaks of the abundance of what accumulates within and issues outward, culminating in the achievement of matching Heaven. Only thus can there be the complete substance of sagely virtue and the ultimate achievement of learning to become a sage. Can sagehood, then, be learned? The answer is simply: first attain clarity in the heart and know where to go; then earnestly put this into practice, seeking to arrive there.

“The goodness of human nature is like water's tendency to flow downward. There is no person who is not good, just as there is no water that does not flow downward.”
Kuang Zongshun

Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “The point that human nature is good and contains nothing that is not good is brought out clearly. This deeply grasps Mencius's intention in awakening his contemporaries [?], and the conclusion especially shows personal understanding. Here is someone with whom one may discuss human nature.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Writing that fully grasps principle naturally has no need of excessive words. This may serve as a model.”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官主事吳批說性善無不善處明白
考試官郎中郭批親切簡當
大賢於人性必發明其有善而無惡也夫有善
無惡性之本體也大賢因時人之言而發明之
則性之本善可知矣昔孟子謂告子曰性善也
不善非性也爾謂性無定體固可使之為善是
蓋溺於意見之偏而不知夫性之本善也蓋人
之為道也仁義之性根於固有而有純粹至善
之妙焉猶夫流水之為物也盈科後進由地中
===
行而有沛然就下之勢焉夫善者人之性下者
水之性水既有必下之性而謂人性本無善豈
可乎哉又謂性無定體亦可使之為不善是蓋
梏於耳目之受而不知夫性之本無不善也蓋
均是性則均是善固無有匪仁匪義而邪焉者
也猶夫同是水則同是下固無有過顙在山而
逆焉者也夫無不善者人之性無不下者水之
性水既無不下之性矣而謂人性有不善又可
乎哉是則性本善也而謂之無分於善本無惡
punctuated:
考試官主事吳批：說性善無不善處明白。

考試官郎中郭批：親切簡當。

大賢於人性，必發明其有善而無惡也。夫有善無惡，性之本體也。大賢因時人之言而發明之，則性之本善可知矣。昔孟子謂告子曰：「性善也，不善非性也。爾謂性無定體，固可使之為善，是蓋溺於意見之偏，而不知夫性之本善也。蓋人之為道也，仁義之性根於固有，而有純粹至善之妙焉。猶夫流水之為物也，盈科後進，由地中行，而有沛然就下之勢焉。夫善者，人之性；下者，水之性。水既有必下之性，而謂人性本無善，豈可乎哉？又謂性無定體，亦可使之為不善，是蓋梏於耳目之受，而不知夫性之本無不善也。蓋均是性，則均是善，固無有匪仁匪義而邪焉者也。猶夫同是水，則同是下，固無有過顙在山而逆焉者也。夫無不善者，人之性；無不下者，水之性。水既無不下之性矣，而謂人性有不善，又可乎哉？」是則性本善也，而謂之無分於善；本無惡
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Secretary, comments: “Clearly explains that human nature is good and contains nothing that is not good.”

Examiner Guo, Director, comments: “Apt, concise, and well judged.”

In discussing human nature, the great worthy necessarily elucidates that it possesses goodness and contains no evil. To possess goodness and contain no evil is the original constitution of human nature. When the great worthy elucidates this in response to the assertions of his contemporaries, the original goodness of human nature becomes apparent. Formerly, Mencius said to Gaozi: “Human nature is good; what is not good is not human nature. You say that human nature has no fixed constitution and can indeed be made good. This is because you are immersed in the partiality of your own views and do not understand the original goodness of human nature. In the human Way, the nature endowed with benevolence and righteousness is rooted in what is inherently possessed and embodies the subtle perfection of pure and utmost goodness. It is like flowing water, which fills hollows before advancing, courses through the earth, and has an abundant impetus to flow downward. Goodness is the nature of human beings; downward flow is the nature of water. Since water has a nature that necessarily flows downward, how can you say that human nature originally possesses no goodness? You also say that human nature has no fixed constitution and can be made not good. This is because you are confined by what your ears and eyes receive and do not understand that human nature originally contains nothing that is not good. Since all share this nature, all share its goodness: there is inherently nothing contrary to benevolence or righteousness and thus perverse within it. Likewise, all water alike flows downward: inherently, none rises above the forehead or remains on a mountain in defiance of its course. To contain nothing that is not good is human nature; never to fail to flow downward is water’s nature. Since water has a nature that never fails to flow downward, how, again, can you say that human nature contains what is not good?” Thus human nature is originally good, yet he says it makes no distinction in favor of goodness; it originally contains no evil …

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也而謂無分於不善孟子以是而折告子可謂
精矣惜乎卒不聞其能自反而有所疑也抑考
善者天地之性也形而後有不善氣質之性也
論性不論氣不備論氣不論性不明孟子之論
天地之性也張子之論輔之以氣質之性也故
孟子發前聖所未發而張子發孟子所未發云
易
乾道變化各正性命保合大和乃利貞
李時言
===
同考試官訓導郭批易義深奥作者先要
明理理明則意到意到則詞暢錄此不獨以其
文而已
同考試官教諭林批詞約理盡瑩潔無瑕
讀之令人有豁然超悟處錄之
考試官主事吳批只用本色語融化可錄
考試官郎中郭批簡潔中有含蓄
大化運而物得其理以自全彖傳釋乾之利貞
也夫物之有成寔大化之運為之也乾之利貞
punctuated:
也，而謂無分於不善。孟子以是而折告子，可謂精矣。惜乎卒不聞其能自反而有所疑也。抑考善者，天地之性也；形而後有不善，氣質之性也。論性不論氣，不備；論氣不論性，不明。孟子之論，天地之性也；張子之論，輔之以氣質之性也。故孟子發前聖所未發，而張子發孟子所未發云。
易
乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。
李時言
同考試官訓導郭批：易義深奥，作者先要明理。理明則意到，意到則詞暢。錄此，不獨以其文而已。
同考試官教諭林批：詞約理盡，瑩潔無瑕。讀之令人有豁然超悟處，錄之。
考試官主事吳批：只用本色語，融化可錄。
考試官郎中郭批：簡潔中有含蓄。
大化運而物得其理以自全，彖傳釋乾之利貞也。夫物之有成，寔大化之運為之也。乾之利貞
translation_en:
…yet he says that it makes no distinction regarding what is not good. Mencius’s use of this argument to refute Gaozi may indeed be called penetrating. Regrettably, we never hear that Gaozi was able to reflect upon himself and come to doubt his position. Further examination shows that goodness belongs to the nature of Heaven and Earth; the presence of what is not good after bodily form comes into being belongs to the nature of the physical constitution. To discuss nature without discussing material force is incomplete; to discuss material force without discussing nature is unclear. Mencius’s discussion concerns the nature of Heaven and Earth; Master Zhang’s discussion supplements it with the nature of the physical constitution. Thus Mencius brought to light what earlier sages had not brought to light, and Master Zhang brought to light what Mencius had not brought to light.

Book of Changes

“The Way of Qian changes and transforms; each thing attains its proper nature and allotted destiny. Preserving and uniting supreme harmony, it is thereby beneficial and steadfast.”

Li Shiyan

Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “The meaning of the Book of Changes is profound. A writer must first understand its principles. When the principles are clear, the thought reaches its mark; when the thought reaches its mark, the language flows freely. This piece is selected for more than its literary merits alone.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The language is concise and the principles fully expressed, luminous and pure, without blemish. Reading it brings moments of sudden, transcendent understanding. Select it.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Secretary: “It uses only natural, unembellished language, thoroughly assimilating its ideas. Worthy of selection.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Director: “Within its concision and clarity, much remains implicit.”

The great process of transformation operates, and things obtain their principles so as to fulfill themselves: this is how the Commentary on the Judgments explains Qian’s being beneficial and steadfast. For the fulfillment of things is indeed brought about by the operation of the great process of transformation. Qian’s being beneficial and steadfast…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
不於是而可見乎吾夫子傳乾之彖而以天道
明之此釋利貞之意若曰天道之元亨固始而
亨矣然而氣序之流行有變以為化之漸流行
之既極有化以為變之成夫乾道變化無所不
利以故萬物之有生者得生理於稟受之初而
不相假借具實理於付畀之始而無少過差秩
然大小之攸宜也自有以各正矣於是冲和之
氣凝於體質之中者詳密而不露會合之精全
於軀幹之内者完固而弗虧充然彼此之具足
===
也不有以保合乎夫如是吾知顯諸仁者藏諸
用氣機之收斂驗諸物理而有徵矣成乎始者
成乎終化工之歸藏觀諸物候而可知矣不謂
之利貞而何是則乾之利貞固有不外乎天道
者彖傳舉而明之其旨精矣抑嘗因是而知造
化相生之妙也是故非元亨以為之先固無以
肇生物之端矣使非利貞以為歸宿之地則蘊
畜無本而天道或幾乎息矣化育之功其何以
亘萬古而如一邪故曰不專一則不能直遂良
punctuated:
不於是而可見乎？吾夫子傳乾之彖，而以天道明之。此釋利貞之意，若曰：天道之元亨，固始而亨矣。然而氣序之流行，有變以為化之漸；流行之既極，有化以為變之成。夫乾道變化，無所不利，以故萬物之有生者，得生理於稟受之初，而不相假借；具實理於付畀之始，而無少過差。秩然大小之攸宜也，自有以各正矣。於是冲和之氣凝於體質之中者，詳密而不露；會合之精全於軀幹之内者，完固而弗虧。充然彼此之具足也，不有以保合乎？夫如是，吾知顯諸仁者藏諸用，氣機之收斂驗諸物理而有徵矣；成乎始者成乎終，化工之歸藏觀諸物候而可知矣。不謂之利貞而何？是則乾之利貞，固有不外乎天道者，彖傳舉而明之，其旨精矣。
抑嘗因是而知造化相生之妙也。是故非元亨以為之先，固無以肇生物之端矣；使非利貞以為歸宿之地，則蘊畜無本，而天道或幾乎息矣。化育之功，其何以亘萬古而如一邪？故曰：「不專一則不能直遂。」良
translation_en:
…is this not where it can be seen? Our Master Confucius, in commenting on the Judgment of Qian, explained it through the Way of Heaven. His explanation of benefit and constancy (li and zhen) means something like this: through origination and flourishing (yuan and heng), the Way of Heaven indeed initiates things and brings them to flourish. Yet as the sequence of vital energies proceeds, there is change that constitutes the gradual approach to transformation; once that progression reaches its limit, there is transformation that constitutes the completion of change. The changes and transformations of the Way of Qian benefit everything. Thus all living things receive their principle of life when first endowed with it, without borrowing from one another; they possess their substantial principle from the moment it is bestowed, without the slightest excess or deficiency. In orderly fashion, each, whether great or small, attains its proper condition. Then the balanced and harmonious vital energy that congeals within their bodily substance is finely integrated and unexposed; the gathered essence preserved within their frames is whole and firm, without diminution. With each and every thing thus fully provided, is there not a means of preserving their unity? In this way, I understand that what is manifest in benevolence is stored within functioning: the gathering inward of the workings of vital energy finds confirmation when tested against the principles of things. What brings accomplishment at the beginning brings accomplishment at the end: the return of the work of transformation to a state of storage can be understood by observing the seasonal conditions of things. What could this be called if not benefit and constancy? Thus Qian’s benefit and constancy are indeed inseparable from the Way of Heaven. The Commentary on the Judgments brings this out and explains it; its meaning is subtle indeed.
Moreover, through this I have come to understand the marvel of creation’s successive generation of things. Without origination and flourishing to come first, there would certainly be no means of initiating the production of things. If benefit and constancy did not provide their final resting place, there would be no foundation for storing and accumulating, and the Way of Heaven might almost cease. How, then, could the work of transformation and nurture remain the same throughout all ages? Hence the saying: “Without concentration and unity, there can be no direct advance.” Truly…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有以也學易者效法天道以求盡乎復性之功
誠能動靜不違而尤必主靜以為之本焉則存
之為天德發之為王道而萬國咸寧之治可以
馴致矣
天地設位聖人成能人謀鬼謀百姓與能
曠宗舜
同考試官訓導郭批此題括盡一部易書
士子深契其旨者不多見此作從容數語而意
味含蓄殆盡宜錄之以為多士式
===
同考試官教諭林批義理得之積學精華
斂於筆端易義如此可與言潔淨精微矣
考試官主事吳批精粹明瑩
考試官郎中郭批詞整意足
聖人本造化以作易有以利民之用焉夫造化
易之原也微聖人易幾乎毀矣民何所利其用
哉大傳論聖人作易之事蓋謂人徒知易為斯
民作也庸詎知其原乎自夫混沌闢而二儀奠
其位陰陽消息之際法象垂焉清濁分而兩間
punctuated:
有以也。學易者效法天道，以求盡乎復性之功，誠能動靜不違，而尤必主靜以為之本焉，則存之為天德，發之為王道，而萬國咸寧之治可以馴致矣。
天地設位，聖人成能，人謀鬼謀，百姓與能。
曠宗舜
同考試官訓導郭批：此題括盡一部易書，士子深契其旨者不多見。此作從容數語，而意味含蓄殆盡，宜錄之以為多士式。
同考試官教諭林批：義理得之積學，精華斂於筆端。易義如此，可與言潔淨精微矣。
考試官主事吳批：精粹明瑩。
考試官郎中郭批：詞整意足。
聖人本造化以作易，有以利民之用焉。夫造化，易之原也。微聖人，易幾乎毀矣，民何所利其用哉？大傳論聖人作易之事，蓋謂人徒知易為斯民作也，庸詎知其原乎？自夫混沌闢，而二儀奠其位，陰陽消息之際，法象垂焉；清濁分，而兩間
translation_en:
…there is good reason for this. Those who study the Changes emulate the Way of Heaven, seeking to complete the work of restoring their nature. If they can truly accord with it in both activity and stillness, and above all take stillness as their foundation, then what they preserve within becomes heavenly virtue, and what they express in action becomes the kingly Way. Thus they may gradually bring about a reign in which all the myriad states enjoy peace.
“Heaven and Earth establish their positions; the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment. People deliberate, spirits deliberate, and the common people participate in these capacities.”
Kuang Zongshun
Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: This topic encompasses the entire Book of Changes. Candidates who deeply grasp its purport are seldom seen. In a few unforced phrases, this composition implicitly conveys almost the whole of its meaning. It should be recorded as a model for the other candidates.
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Its principles have been grasped through accumulated learning, and their essence is concentrated at the tip of the brush. With an exposition of the Changes like this, one may indeed discuss purity, refinement, and subtlety.
Comment by Examiner Wu, Secretary: Refined and essential, clear and luminous.
Comment by Examiner Guo, Director: Well-ordered wording and fully expressed meaning.
The sage based his composition of the Changes on the processes of creation and transformation, thereby providing something beneficial for the people's use. Creation and transformation are the source of the Changes. Without the sage, the Changes would all but have been lost; how could the people have benefited from its use? In discussing the sage's composition of the Changes, the Great Commentary suggests that people know only that the Changes was composed for them: how could they know its source? Once primordial chaos opened and the two powers, Heaven and Earth, established their positions, models and images were displayed amid the waning and waxing of yin and yang; the clear and the turbid separated, and between Heaven and Earth…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
運其化剛柔進退之中至教寓焉由是聖人有
作觀文察理畫卦爻以闡秘而險易陳其端窮
神知化係辭占以盡言而憂患明其故是天地
之所欲言而未能者聖人爲之成之矣夫易不
作則民貿貿焉爾乃今行而有疑既先爰咨爰
諏就人謀以審其可否謀而未定則必以筮以
卜假鬼謀以斷其成敗由是百姓雖曰至愚然
幾有以開其先而所向不迷擬議成變化之功
事有以啓其衷而有爲不怠變通盡出入之利
===
是聖人之所以能前知者百姓亦得以與之矣
是知易書之作其原出於造化其功及于斯民
聖人之能事豈復有餘哉雖然三才一道八卦
一理天地先之聖人發之衆人用之故易之書
遠如天近如地神用而不窮妙應而不測其斯
所以爲易乎後世作潛虛太玄以擬易者其僭
侮聖經甚矣噫其亦何庸損于易
書
五月南巡守至于南岳如岱禮八月西巡
punctuated:
運其化，剛柔進退之中，至教寓焉。由是聖人有作，觀文察理，畫卦爻以闡秘，而險易陳其端；窮神知化，係辭占以盡言，而憂患明其故。是天地之所欲言而未能者，聖人爲之成之矣。夫易不作，則民貿貿焉爾。乃今行而有疑，既先爰咨爰諏，就人謀以審其可否；謀而未定，則必以筮以卜，假鬼謀以斷其成敗。由是百姓雖曰至愚，然幾有以開其先，而所向不迷，擬議成變化之功；事有以啓其衷，而有爲不怠，變通盡出入之利。是聖人之所以能前知者，百姓亦得以與之矣。是知易書之作，其原出於造化，其功及于斯民，聖人之能事豈復有餘哉？雖然，三才一道，八卦一理，天地先之，聖人發之，衆人用之。故易之書，遠如天，近如地，神用而不窮，妙應而不測，其斯所以爲易乎？後世作《潛虛》《太玄》以擬易者，其僭侮聖經甚矣！噫，其亦何庸損于易？

書

五月南巡守，至于南岳，如岱禮。八月西巡
translation_en:
…carry out their transformations; within the advance and retreat of the firm and yielding, the highest teachings reside. Thus the sage arose: observing patterns and examining principles, he drew the hexagrams and their lines to reveal what was hidden, displaying the beginnings of danger and ease. Plumbing the spiritual and understanding transformation, he attached statements and prognostications to give full expression to their meaning, making clear the causes of anxiety and trouble. What Heaven and Earth wished to express but could not, the sage thus brought to completion for them.

Had the Changes not been made, the people would merely have remained bewildered. Now, when they have doubts about taking action, they first seek advice and inquire, consulting others to judge whether it is permissible. If consultation leaves the matter undecided, they must divine with milfoil stalks and turtle shells, drawing on the counsel of spirits to determine success or failure. Thus, although the common people may be called utterly ignorant, incipient signs can give them advance understanding, so that they are not confused about their direction; through comparison and deliberation, they accomplish the work of transformation. In affairs, their inner understanding can be awakened, so that they act without slackening; through adaptation, they realize all the benefits of going forth and coming in. The means by which the sage can know beforehand thus become something in which the common people, too, can share.

We know from this that the making of the book of Changes had its source in the creative transformations of the cosmos, while its achievements extended to the people. What more could remain for the sage to accomplish? Nevertheless, the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—share one Way, and the eight trigrams share one principle. Heaven and Earth initiate it, the sage reveals it, and ordinary people put it to use. Thus the book of Changes is as distant as Heaven and as near as Earth; its spiritual operation is inexhaustible, and its wondrous responses unfathomable. Is this not what makes it the Changes? Those in later ages who composed the Concealed Void (Qianxu) and the Supreme Mystery (Taixuan) in imitation of the Changes showed extreme presumption and disrespect toward the sage’s classic! Alas, how could they diminish the Changes?

Book of Documents

“In the fifth month, he made a tour of inspection southward, reaching the Southern Sacred Peak and observing the rites used at Mount Dai. In the eighth month, he made a tour westward…”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
守至于西岳如初十有一月朔巡守至
于北岳如西禮歸格于藝祖用特五載
一巡守群后四朝敷奏以言明試以功
車服以庸
胡彥
同考試官教諭陳批巡守述職二者治體
最大非有大識見者未能如此形容
同考試官學正陳批此篇鋪張巡守述職
之典儼若躬際虞廷之盛者佳作也
===
考試官主事吳批讀此可想見虞廷之盛
考試官郎中郭批典雅可式
聖人舉時巡之禮而歸告於祖者其禮隆定朝
巡之期而統御乎臣者其法備蓋巡守述職人
君致治之大端也大舜攝位而舉行之其知治
體者與昔舜受攝位之命適巡守之期故五月
而南至於南岳祀禮舉之諸侯覲之正朔一之
禮則岱宗之禮也制度同之五禮修之五器如
之政則東巡之政也由是自夏而秋自南而西
punctuated:
守，至于西岳，如初。十有一月朔，巡守至于北岳，如西禮。歸，格于藝祖，用特。五載一巡守，群后四朝。敷奏以言，明試以功，車服以庸。
胡彥
同考試官教諭陳批：巡守、述職二者，治體最大，非有大識見者，未能如此形容。
同考試官學正陳批：此篇鋪張巡守、述職之典，儼若躬際虞廷之盛者，佳作也。
考試官主事吳批：讀此，可想見虞廷之盛。
考試官郎中郭批：典雅可式。
聖人舉時巡之禮而歸告於祖者，其禮隆；定朝巡之期而統御乎臣者，其法備。蓋巡守、述職，人君致治之大端也。大舜攝位而舉行之，其知治體者與！昔舜受攝位之命，適巡守之期，故五月而南至於南岳。祀禮舉之，諸侯覲之，正朔一之，禮則岱宗之禮也；制度同之，五禮修之，五器如之，政則東巡之政也。由是，自夏而秋，自南而西，
translation_en:
…on his tour of inspection, he reached the Western Sacred Peak and observed the same rites as before. On the first day of the eleventh month, he toured to the Northern Sacred Peak and observed the same rites as in the west. Returning, he presented himself at the temple of his founding ancestor and offered a single bull. Once every five years he made a tour of inspection, and the various lords came to court four times. They gave full verbal reports; he openly tested them by their accomplishments and awarded carriages and robes according to their service.
Hu Yan 胡彥
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Tours of inspection and reports on duties are two matters of the greatest importance in the ordering of government. Without great insight, one could not describe them in this way.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor in a subprefectural Confucian school: “This essay expansively sets forth the institutions of inspection tours and reports on duties, as though its author had personally witnessed the flourishing court of Shun. An excellent work.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Secretary: “Reading this, one can picture the flourishing court of Shun.”
Comment by Examiner Guo, Director: “Classical and elegant, worthy of being taken as a model.”
When the sage performed the rites of seasonal inspection tours and returned to report to his ancestor, his ritual observance was exalted; when he fixed the intervals for court audiences and inspection tours and thereby governed his ministers, his regulations were complete. For inspection tours and reports on duties are fundamental means by which a ruler achieves good government. The great Shun put them into practice upon assuming the regency: surely he understood the essentials of government!
Formerly, when Shun received the command to assume the regency, the time for an inspection tour had arrived. Thus, in the fifth month he traveled south to the Southern Sacred Peak. He performed the sacrificial rites, received the feudal lords in audience, and unified the calendar: these rites were those observed at Daizong. He standardized institutions and measures, put the five rites in order, and brought the five ceremonial jade tokens into conformity: these administrative acts were those of his eastern tour. From this point, as summer passed into autumn and he traveled from south to west, …

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
則至于西岳矣儀文之典政事之施者西固猶
夫東焉由是自秋而冬自西而北則至于北岳
矣儀文之典政事之施者北固猶夫西焉于是
薄言旋歸京師至止格廟以反面致其如在之
誠特牛以將事示其無文之敬其巡守之禮蓋
如此又以歲序易更人心或懈五載之内天子
巡守者一上情得以下達諸侯來朝者四下情
得以上通敷奏以言以觀其蘊而因言知政幽
隱皆得以畢達明試以功以考其成而聽言觀
===
行殿最不得以或逃有功則賜之輅車乘馬以
安其體使有功者於是而益勸玄袞及黼以華
其躬使無功者因是而知勉其朝巡之禮蓋如
此是則朝巡之制立而統御之法周上下相承
體統不紊有虞之治所以不可及與抑易有之
天地交而萬物通上下交而其志同也故古之
君臣分嚴而情親勢疏而心密觀之唐虞槩可
見矣後世尊君卑臣之制立而是禮不復講矣
惜哉
punctuated: 則至于西岳矣。儀文之典、政事之施者，西固猶夫東焉。由是自秋而冬，自西而北，則至于北岳矣。儀文之典、政事之施者，北固猶夫西焉。于是薄言旋歸，京師至止，格廟以反面，致其如在之誠；特牛以將事，示其無文之敬。其巡守之禮蓋如此。又以歲序易更，人心或懈，五載之内，天子巡守者一，上情得以下達；諸侯來朝者四，下情得以上通。敷奏以言，以觀其蘊，而因言知政，幽隱皆得以畢達；明試以功，以考其成，而聽言觀行，殿最不得以或逃。有功則賜之輅車乘馬，以安其體，使有功者於是而益勸；玄袞及黼，以華其躬，使無功者因是而知勉。其朝巡之禮蓋如此。是則朝巡之制立，而統御之法周，上下相承，體統不紊，有虞之治所以不可及與！抑《易》有之：「天地交而萬物通，上下交而其志同也。」故古之君臣，分嚴而情親，勢疏而心密。觀之唐虞，槩可見矣。後世尊君卑臣之制立，而是禮不復講矣。惜哉！
translation_en:
…he then reached the Western Sacred Peak. In its ceremonial observances and the administration of government, the west was indeed like the east. Then, passing from autumn into winter and from west to north, he reached the Northern Sacred Peak. In its ceremonial observances and the administration of government, the north was indeed like the west. Thereupon he returned and arrived at the capital. He entered the ancestral temple to report his return, expressing his sincerity as though the ancestors were present; he offered a single ox in performing the service, displaying his unadorned reverence. Such were the rites of his inspection tours.

Moreover, because the years passed in succession and people’s resolve might slacken, within each five-year period the Son of Heaven made one inspection tour, enabling the concerns of those above to reach those below; the regional lords came to court four times, enabling the concerns of those below to reach those above. He had them present their reports in words, to examine what lay within them and learn of their government through their statements, so that even hidden matters could all be fully conveyed. He openly tested them through their achievements, to assess what they had accomplished; by listening to their words and observing their conduct, he ensured that neither the worst nor the best performance could escape scrutiny. Those with merit were granted state carriages and teams of four horses for their bodily comfort, so that the meritorious would be still further encouraged; dark dragon-patterned robes and robes with axe-patterned embroidery adorned their persons, so that those without merit would thereby learn to exert themselves. Such were the rites of court audiences and inspection tours.

Thus, with the system of court audiences and inspection tours established, the methods of governing and directing his subjects were complete. Those above and below sustained one another, and the order of government remained undisturbed. Surely this explains why the government of Youyu—that is, Shun—could not be surpassed! Furthermore, the Book of Changes says: “Heaven and earth interact, and the myriad things communicate; those above and below interact, and their purposes are one.” Thus, among the rulers and ministers of antiquity, distinctions of rank were strict, yet their feelings were close; their positions were far apart, yet their hearts were intimate. Looking at Tang and Yu—the ages of Yao and Shun—we can see the broad outlines of this. In later ages, a system that exalted rulers and abased ministers became established, and these rites were no longer cultivated. What a pity!

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
三后協心同底于道
郭謙
同考試官教諭陳批協心同道此周家善
處殷民之術子能命詞而發其意是亦可與語
治者
同考試官學正陳批心道二字多講不明
此作詞意明整是宜錄出
考試官主事吳批康王屬望本意此作得之
考試官郎中郭批文有體式
===
賢王於大臣既言其同前臣之治本復言其同
前臣之治具蓋心者治之本也道者治之具也
三后協之同之其於治也何有康王期畢公意
謂天下之治莫善於同而化殷之道尤恐其異
公與二公其有合哉是故存諸中者之謂心而
三后協之謹始和中成終政雖有不同也皆能
即其行事而濟其事有若成於一人觀其用心
而濟其心有若出於一時公後二公而生未至
而難料也二公則若豫見乎公而已逆與之合
punctuated:
三后協心，同底于道。
郭謙

同考試官教諭陳批：「協心同道，此周家善處殷民之術。子能命詞而發其意，是亦可與語治者。」
同考試官學正陳批：「心、道二字，多講不明。此作詞意明整，是宜錄出。」
考試官主事吳批：「康王屬望本意，此作得之。」
考試官郎中郭批：「文有體式。」

賢王於大臣，既言其同前臣之治本，復言其同前臣之治具。蓋心者，治之本也；道者，治之具也。三后協之同之，其於治也何有？康王期畢公，意謂天下之治莫善於同，而化殷之道尤恐其異。公與二公，其有合哉！是故存諸中者之謂心，而三后協之。謹始、和中、成終，政雖有不同也，皆能即其行事而濟其事，有若成於一人；觀其用心而濟其心，有若出於一時。公後二公而生，未至而難料也，二公則若豫見乎公，而已逆與之合。
translation_en:
“The three lords united their hearts and together attained the Way.”
Guo Qian

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Uniting their hearts and following the same Way: this was the Zhou house’s art of dealing well with the people of Yin. You have been able to frame your words to bring out its meaning. You, too, are someone with whom one may discuss government.”
Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: “The two terms ‘heart’ and ‘Way’ are often explained unclearly. This composition is clear and orderly in wording and meaning, and deserves to be selected for inclusion.”
Examiner Wu, Secretary, comments: “This composition captures the original intent of King Kang’s expression of his expectations.”
Examiner Guo, Director, comments: “The composition has proper form.”

Addressing his great minister, the worthy king had already spoken of his sharing the foundations of government with earlier ministers; he then spoke of his sharing their means of government as well. For the heart is the foundation of government, and the Way is its means. With the three lords united in the former and at one in the latter, what difficulty could there be in governing? In setting his expectations for the Duke of Bi, King Kang meant that nothing was better for governing all under Heaven than concord, and that, in transforming the people of Yin, divergence was especially to be feared. Surely the duke and the two other dukes were in accord!

Thus, what is held within is called the heart, and the three lords united in it. Exercising care at the beginning, fostering harmony in the middle, and bringing the undertaking to completion at the end: although their administrations differed, each could carry forward the others’ deeds through his own actions, as though everything had been accomplished by one person. Looking at how they applied their hearts and fulfilled one another’s intentions, it was as though these had arisen at a single time. The duke was born after the two other dukes; what had not yet come to pass was difficult to foresee. Yet the two dukes seemed to have foreseen him and already to have been in accord with him beforehand…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
二公先公而生已往而難知也公則追考乎二
公而亦暗與之孚謹始者此心和中者此心成
終者亦此心也所謂協心者非歟至若施之於
外之謂道而三后同之始之中之終之事若有
不同也但以道有升降拘於勢之必然政由俗
革質之道而皆合撫世酬物同夫致理之宜二
公之道猶夫公也稱物平施均之適治之路我
公之道猶夫二公也謹始者此道和中者此道
成終者亦此道也所謂同道者非歟是則三后
===
協心則內之所存者無異思同底于道則外之
所施者無異法化頑之方斯其至矣於乎武王
成康何君也周畢君陳何臣也君臣一心先後
一道非直三公之協且同而已也乃能化頑成
仁民用攸勸不然則商人之洶洶尚未可知也
雖然於此亦可以見商先哲王之德之入人之
深也在周視之為頑在商則不失為義矣
詩
釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣告于文人錫山土田
punctuated:
二公先公而生，已往而難知也，公則追考乎二公，而亦暗與之孚。謹始者此心，和中者此心，成終者亦此心也。所謂協心者非歟？至若施之於外之謂道，而三后同之。始之、中之、終之，事若有不同也，但以道有升降，拘於勢之必然，政由俗革，質之道而皆合。撫世酬物，同夫致理之宜，二公之道猶夫公也；稱物平施，均之適治之路，我公之道猶夫二公也。謹始者此道，和中者此道，成終者亦此道也。所謂同道者非歟？是則三后協心，則內之所存者無異思；同底于道，則外之所施者無異法。化頑之方，斯其至矣！於乎！武王、成、康何君也！周、畢、君陳何臣也！君臣一心，先後一道，非直三公之協且同而已也。乃能化頑成仁，民用攸勸。不然，則商人之洶洶尚未可知也。雖然，於此亦可以見商先哲王之德之入人之深也。在周視之為頑，在商則不失為義矣。

詩

釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣，告于文人，錫山土田。
translation_en:
…The two dukes lived before you; their time had passed and was difficult to know. Yet you examined their deeds retrospectively and likewise accorded with them without direct contact. The heart that exercised care at the beginning, that brought harmony in the middle, and that completed the work at the end was the same heart. Is this not what is meant by being united in heart? As for what is put into outward practice, this is called the Way, and the three lords shared it. Their undertakings at the beginning, middle, and end might seem different, but this was only because the Way’s practice rose or fell under the unavoidable constraints of circumstances, and policies changed with customs. Measured against the Way, all were in accord. In tending to the age and responding to affairs, they shared the proper means of achieving order: the Way of the two dukes was like yours. In weighing circumstances and administering measures equitably, they equally followed the path toward good government: your Way, my lord, was like that of the two dukes. The Way that exercised care at the beginning, that brought harmony in the middle, and that completed the work at the end was the same Way. Is this not what is meant by sharing the Way?

Thus, when the three lords were united in heart, the thoughts they harbored within did not differ; when they arrived together at the Way, the methods they applied outwardly did not differ. Here the means of transforming the recalcitrant reached their utmost perfection! Ah! What rulers were Kings Wu, Cheng, and Kang! What ministers were the Duke of Zhou, the Duke of Bi, and Jun Chen! Rulers and ministers shared one heart, and predecessors and successors followed one Way. It was not merely that the three lords were united and acted alike. Thus they could transform the recalcitrant and bring them to benevolence, and the people were thereby encouraged to do good. Otherwise, there is no knowing what turmoil the people of Shang might have caused. Nevertheless, this also shows how deeply the virtue of Shang’s former wise kings had entered people’s hearts. From Zhou’s perspective, these people were regarded as recalcitrant; in relation to Shang, however, they could still be considered righteous.

Book of Odes

“I bestow upon you a jade-handled libation ladle and one you-vessel of fragrant black-millet sacrificial wine. Make announcement to your illustrious ancestors. I grant you mountains, lands, and fields…”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
于周受命自召祖命虎拜稽首天子萬
年虎拜稽首對揚王休作召公考天子
萬壽明明天子令聞不已矢其文德洽
此四國
周采
同考試官訓導余批此詩前一章詩旨明
白至後章末四句亦是勒銘之詞學者往往掉
開說去甚戾本旨殊不知恃功者易驕用武者
易黷召公恐宣王之驕且黷也故美其令聞而
===
進以不已仍以矢文德洽四國勸之此忠君第
一義當時對揚之本心正在此乎獨能言之而
公之心益白錄之不獨以其文也
同考試官教諭周批宣王賞功之典召公
愛君之心盡於此詩而形容簡當盡於此作是
宜錄之以式來學
考試官主事吳批斂繁于約自是作手
考試官郎中郭批雅健
大臣受君賜而祝之至彰君賜而望之深蓋君
punctuated:
于周受命，自召祖命。虎拜稽首：「天子萬年！」虎拜稽首，對揚王休，作召公考：「天子萬壽！明明天子，令聞不已，矢其文德，洽此四國。」
周采。
同考試官訓導余批：「此詩前一章，詩旨明白。至後章末四句，亦是勒銘之詞，學者往往掉開說去，甚戾本旨。殊不知恃功者易驕，用武者易黷。召公恐宣王之驕且黷也，故美其令聞而進以不已，仍以矢文德、洽四國勸之。此忠君第一義，當時對揚之本心正在此乎！獨能言之，而公之心益白。錄之，不獨以其文也。」
同考試官教諭周批：「宣王賞功之典，召公愛君之心，盡於此詩；而形容簡當，盡於此作。是宜錄之，以式來學。」
考試官主事吳批：「斂繁于約，自是作手。」
考試官郎中郭批：「雅健。」
大臣受君賜而祝之至，彰君賜而望之深。蓋君
translation_en:
…Receive the charge at Zhou, following the charge given to your ancestor, the Duke of Shao. Hu bowed and knocked his head to the ground: “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!” Hu bowed and knocked his head to the ground, gratefully extolling the king’s favor, and made a shrine to the Duke of Shao [?]: “May the Son of Heaven enjoy ten thousand years of life! May the illustrious Son of Heaven’s good fame never cease! May he display his civil virtue and bring harmony to the states of the four quarters.”
Zhou Cai.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: “The meaning of the first stanza of this poem is clear. The last four lines of the following stanza are likewise words engraved as an inscription. Students often turn away from this and pursue another explanation, seriously departing from the original meaning. They fail to understand that those who rely on their achievements readily become arrogant, and those who employ military force readily become reckless in its use. The Duke of Shao feared that King Xuan would become both arrogant and reckless. He therefore praised the king’s good fame, then urged that it never cease, and further exhorted him to display his civil virtue and bring harmony to the states of the four quarters. This is the foremost principle of loyalty to one’s ruler. Surely this was precisely his underlying intention when he gratefully extolled the royal favor! This writer alone has managed to express it, making the duke’s intention still clearer. We select this answer not merely for its literary merit.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “King Xuan’s ceremony of rewarding achievement and the Duke of Shao’s loving concern for his ruler are fully expressed in this poem; their concise and apt depiction is fully achieved in this essay. It deserves selection as a model for future students.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Secretary: “He condenses the complex into the concise: clearly an accomplished writer.”
Comment by Examiner Guo, Director: “Elegant and vigorous.”
When a great minister receives his ruler’s gifts, his wishes for the ruler’s well-being are most earnest; when he makes those gifts manifest, his hopes for the ruler are profound. For the ruler’s …

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賜所以報有功也大臣受之而致其祝望焉忠
愛之情蔑以加矣昔宣王命召穆公平淮夷詩
人美之至此意謂江漢之功虎既成矣王錫之
策其詞維何蓋我有圭瓚秬鬯一卣則於爾釐
之以供乎祀維山土田告我文祖則於爾錫之
以廣其封又命召虎言往于岐式承我之寵賚
以爾先祖受命玆土爰表爾之世功於是虎也
致拜稽于天子祝壽考於萬年握瑶圖而主百
神克享無疆之慶負丹扆而朝群后永綏戩穀
===
之休其受策于朝而祝之至也如此夫虎既受
策載展拜稽之恭對揚休美之命作彼彛器置
諸康公之廟勒玆命詞考我武功之成又祝以
維天錫嘏俾我天子享眉壽于益綿維王受祉
與玆軌物歷永世而不朽於是虎也復致明明
之稱於天子以為禍亂既戡厥聲亦既昭矣又
必庶幾夙夜不已其令聞可焉武功告成修文
維其時矣又必丕揚德教周徧于四國可焉其
銘器于廟而望之深也如此是則祝之至者感
punctuated:
賜所以報有功也。大臣受之而致其祝望焉，忠愛之情蔑以加矣。昔宣王命召穆公平淮夷，詩人美之，至此意謂：江漢之功，虎既成矣。王錫之策，其詞維何？蓋我有圭瓚、秬鬯一卣，則於爾釐之，以供乎祀；維山土田，告我文祖，則於爾錫之，以廣其封。又命召虎，言往于岐，式承我之寵賚，以爾先祖受命玆土，爰表爾之世功。於是虎也致拜稽于天子，祝壽考於萬年：握瑶圖而主百神，克享無疆之慶；負丹扆而朝群后，永綏戩穀之休。其受策于朝而祝之至也如此。
夫虎既受策，載展拜稽之恭，對揚休美之命，作彼彛器，置諸康公之廟，勒玆命詞，考我武功之成。又祝以維天錫嘏，俾我天子享眉壽于益綿；維王受祉，與玆軌物歷永世而不朽。於是虎也復致明明之稱於天子，以為禍亂既戡，厥聲亦既昭矣，又必庶幾夙夜不已其令聞可焉；武功告成，修文維其時矣，又必丕揚德教，周徧于四國可焉。其銘器于廟而望之深也如此。是則祝之至者，感
translation_en:
…bestowals serve to reward those who have rendered meritorious service. When a great minister receives them and expresses his blessings and hopes for his ruler, no feeling of loyalty and love could surpass his. In former times, King Xuan commanded Duke Mu of Shao to pacify the Huaiyi, and the poet praised him. At this point, the poem means that Hu had completed his achievements in the Jiang and Han region. What were the words of the document the king bestowed upon him? They were, in substance: “I have a jade-handled libation ladle and a vessel of aromatic black-millet wine; I grant these to you for use in sacrifices. As for the mountains and lands, I have reported the matter to my cultured ancestor and bestow them upon you to enlarge your fief.” He further commanded Shao Hu: “Go to Qi and receive my gracious gifts. Since your ancestor received his charge in this land, I thereby honor the achievements of your lineage.” Hu then bowed and touched his forehead to the ground before the Son of Heaven, wishing him a long life of ten thousand years: “May you hold the precious chart of sovereignty and preside over the hundred spirits, enjoying blessings without limit; may you sit before the vermilion screen and receive the homage of the assembled lords, forever enjoying the blessings of happiness and good fortune.” Such was the utmost devotion of his blessings when he received the royal document at court.
Having received the document, Hu again displayed his reverence by bowing and touching his forehead to the ground. In grateful acknowledgment and celebration of the gracious command, he had ritual vessels made and placed them in the temple of Duke Kang. He engraved the words of this command upon them to commemorate the completion of his military achievements. He further offered this blessing: “May Heaven confer blessings, allowing our Son of Heaven to enjoy an ever longer life. May the king receive good fortune and, together with these exemplary objects, endure through endless generations without decay.” Hu then again praised the Son of Heaven as illustrious, considering that, although calamity and disorder had been quelled and the king’s reputation had already become brilliant, he must still strive, morning and night, never to cease sustaining his good name. With military achievements accomplished, the time had come to cultivate civil governance; he must further spread moral instruction widely, extending it throughout the four quarters. Such was the depth of his hopes when he inscribed the vessels in the ancestral temple. Thus, the utmost devotion of his blessings arose from gratitude…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之至也望之深者愛之深也宣王所以得此于
其臣者豈偶然哉大抵君臣休戚關乎一體故
祝望者忠愛之至情規戒者憂危之深慮皆不
可無也宣王克平諸夷中興之業可謂盛矣召
公拳拳于令聞文治之箴豈直爲感謝發邪噫
後世志怠于平吳功隳于克蔡者其亦未聞召
公之訓與
受小球大球爲下國綴旒何天之休
范永官
===
同考試官訓導余批講綴旒處親切有味
末句尤善發揮且無一語蹈襲陳言可愛可傳
同考試官教諭周批發天與人歸意明白
而氣亦充贍錄之
考試官主事吳批寓精采於冲淡可錄
考試官郎中郭批得詩人頌體
聖王朝群后而繫其心所以承天之眷也蓋人
心之歸天意所在也商王所以得此者謂非敬
德所致哉詩人頌美之意蓋謂維我成湯以一
punctuated:
之至也，望之深者愛之深也。宣王所以得此于其臣者，豈偶然哉？大抵君臣休戚關乎一體，故祝望者忠愛之至情，規戒者憂危之深慮，皆不可無也。宣王克平諸夷，中興之業可謂盛矣。召公拳拳于令聞文治之箴，豈直爲感謝發邪？噫！後世志怠于平吳，功隳于克蔡者，其亦未聞召公之訓與？
受小球大球，爲下國綴旒，何天之休。
范永官
同考試官訓導余批：講綴旒處，親切有味。末句尤善發揮，且無一語蹈襲陳言，可愛可傳。
同考試官教諭周批：發天與人歸意，明白而氣亦充贍，錄之。
考試官主事吳批：寓精采於冲淡，可錄。
考試官郎中郭批：得詩人頌體。
聖王朝群后而繫其心，所以承天之眷也。蓋人心之歸，天意所在也。商王所以得此者，謂非敬德所致哉？詩人頌美之意，蓋謂維我成湯以一
translation_en:
…the utmost depth of feeling; profound expectations express profound love. Could King Xuan have received such devotion from his minister merely by chance? Generally speaking, ruler and ministers share good fortune and adversity as one body. Thus blessings and expectations express the deepest loyalty and love, while admonitions express profound concern about danger. Neither can be dispensed with. King Xuan subdued the various foreign peoples, and his achievement in restoring the dynasty may indeed be called magnificent. Yet the Duke of Shao remained earnest in admonishing him to maintain his good reputation and cultivate civil governance. Could these words have arisen merely from gratitude? Alas! Those in later ages whose resolve slackened after pacifying Wu, or whose accomplishments crumbled after conquering Cai—had they perhaps never heard the Duke of Shao’s admonition?
“He receives the small jade orbs and the large jade orbs; he is the support to which the states below attach themselves like banner streamers; he bears Heaven’s blessing.”
Fan Yongguan
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: “The discussion of ‘the support to which they attach themselves like banner streamers’ is apt and rich in meaning. The final phrase is developed especially well. Moreover, not a single expression repeats stale language. Worth cherishing and passing on.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “It clearly brings out the meaning of Heaven’s favor and the people’s allegiance, and its expressive force is also ample. Include it.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Secretary: “It embeds brilliance within a restrained simplicity. Worth including.”
Comment by Examiner Guo, Director: “It captures the poet’s manner of praise.”
The sage king receives the assembled lords at court and binds their hearts to him: this is how he receives Heaven’s favor. For where the people’s hearts turn is where Heaven’s intent resides. Could one say that the king of Shang attained this through anything other than reverent cultivation of virtue? The poet’s intention in offering praise is, in essence, to say that our Cheng Tang, through a single…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
德之純而爲九圍之式于何見之觀其坐明堂
以朝諸侯秉玉而入覲者有小國也小球受焉
其獻享之敬有却之而弗能者矣居南面以臨
百辟執瑞而聽命者有大國也大球受焉其歸
嚮之誠有違之而弗克者矣之綱之紀而聯屬
乎萬方如縿在旆旒實綴之渙焉者有萃聚之
勢會極歸極而維繫于一人如旆有旒維縿是
綴散焉者有合一之機夫天命難諶每驗于人
心之去留人心既得自獲夫上天之眷注冥默
===
之中而保祐存焉四海之格萬福之攸萃也湯
其有以祗承之矣赫臨之下而黙相寓焉萬方
之同百祥之攸集也湯其有以克荷之矣觀此
則知天人之際感通無間而成湯福德之盛所
以隆有商之業者不在是與抑論德者福之本
敬者德之聚有商之業肇於受國是達愙於海
外有截而盛于九圍之命原其本則率履不越
者實基之矣聖敬日躋特光大之耳噫使後之
子孫勿替引焉商雖至今存可也詩人雖以頌
punctuated: 德之純而爲九圍之式，于何見之？觀其坐明堂以朝諸侯，秉玉而入覲者有小國也，小球受焉，其獻享之敬有却之而弗能者矣。居南面以臨百辟，執瑞而聽命者有大國也，大球受焉，其歸嚮之誠有違之而弗克者矣。之綱之紀而聯屬乎萬方，如縿在旆，旒實綴之，渙焉者有萃聚之勢；會極歸極而維繫于一人，如旆有旒，維縿是綴，散焉者有合一之機。夫天命難諶，每驗于人心之去留。人心既得，自獲夫上天之眷注。冥默之中而保祐存焉，四海之格，萬福之攸萃也，湯其有以祗承之矣；赫臨之下而黙相寓焉，萬方之同，百祥之攸集也，湯其有以克荷之矣。觀此，則知天人之際感通無間，而成湯福德之盛，所以隆有商之業者，不在是與？抑論德者福之本，敬者德之聚。有商之業，肇於受國是達，愙於海外有截，而盛于九圍之命。原其本，則率履不越者實基之矣，聖敬日躋特光大之耳。噫！使後之子孫勿替引焉，商雖至今存可也。詩人雖以頌
translation_en:
…through the purity of his virtue became a model for the nine regions. Where can this be seen? Consider him seated in the Hall of Enlightenment, receiving the feudal lords in audience. Among those who enter bearing jade are rulers of small states: he accepts their small jade globes. Their reverence in presenting offerings is such that he could not turn them away. Facing south, he presides over the many lords. Among those who bear jade credentials and await his commands are rulers of great states: he accepts their great jade globes. Their sincere allegiance is such that he could not reject it.
