Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Whether the Classic of Rites is complete or deficient depends on the person: this is an insight independently attained. Should someone recognize your abilities, you may proceed on this principle.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Secretary: “Both talent and discernment are excellent. Worth selecting.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Director: “Amid his extensive learning there is sound judgment: he is a man of outstanding discernment. His other compositions are all excellent; this one has been selected simply as a representative example.”

When reading the sages’ classics after they have fallen into disorder, one should comprehend their essential purpose; when applying the sages’ classics after parts have been lost, one should take their intent as one’s guide. Are the classics indeed complete? I do not know. If one reads them without grasping their essential purpose, then even completeness is as good as deficiency. Are the classics indeed free of disorder? I do not know. If one applies them without taking their intent as one’s guide, then even freedom from disorder is as good as disorder. Comprehending their essential purpose, one understands their rites through their differences and similarities, and brings their ceremonies into accord with the proper degrees of elaboration and simplicity. Taking their intent as one’s guide, one does not cling rigidly to their wording in …

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
又遠而同其政於和平是故經之亂匪經
亂也人亂之也經之全匪經全也人全之
也讀易而至於韋編三絕豈記誦於言語
者乎一言而誦之終身豈習說於詞章者
乎若夫后世之誦經者以贓敗擬易者以
諛名元凱失左氏之意孔光柳宗元之不
識字是皆爲讀書而不會其心者矣尚何
望聖經之全乎執事以三禮下詢承學愚
敢曰會其心可也師其意可也三禮者何
===
周禮儀禮禮記是矣周禮之爲書也備體
國經野之規建官分職之義誠哉周公致
太平之書也奈之何封建之制不與王制
合建都之制不與洛誥合則曰此文王治
岐之書成周理財之書也見九畿之制不
與禹貢合六官之制不與周官合則曰此
戰國陰謀之書漢儒附會之書也亦何不
思之甚也及至劉歆以考工記補之遂至
不可致詰而冬官若亡矣故先儒謂聖經
punctuated:
又遠而同其政於和平。是故經之亂，匪經亂也，人亂之也；經之全，匪經全也，人全之也。讀易而至於韋編三絕，豈記誦於言語者乎？一言而誦之終身，豈習說於詞章者乎？若夫后世之誦經者以贓敗，擬易者以諛名，元凱失左氏之意，孔光柳宗元之不識字，是皆爲讀書而不會其心者矣，尚何望聖經之全乎？執事以三禮下詢承學，愚敢曰：會其心可也，師其意可也。

三禮者何？周禮、儀禮、禮記是矣。周禮之爲書也，備體國經野之規、建官分職之義，誠哉周公致太平之書也！奈之何封建之制不與王制合，建都之制不與洛誥合，則曰：「此文王治岐之書，成周理財之書也。」見九畿之制不與禹貢合，六官之制不與周官合，則曰：「此戰國陰謀之書，漢儒附會之書也。」亦何不思之甚也！及至劉歆以考工記補之，遂至不可致詰，而冬官若亡矣。故先儒謂聖經
translation_en:
…in the distant past [?], and bring its government into accord with peace and harmony. Thus, disorder in the Classics is not disorder inherent in them: people have disordered them. Completeness in the Classics is not completeness inherent in them: people make them complete. When someone reads the Changes until the leather binding cords break three times, can he be merely memorizing and reciting words? When someone recites a single saying throughout his life, can he be merely rehearsing explanations and literary compositions? Yet among later generations, those who recited the Classics were disgraced for corruption, and those who imitated the Changes became notorious for flattery. Yuankai missed the meaning of Master Zuo; Kong Guang and Liu Zongyuan failed to understand the written word. These were all readers who failed to grasp the heart of what they read. How, then, could one still hope for the completeness of the sages’ Classics? You, honored examiners, have condescended to question us students about the Three Ritual Classics. I venture to reply: grasp their heart, and take their intent as your guide.

What are the Three Ritual Classics? They are the Rites of Zhou, the Ceremonies and Rites, and the Record of Rites. The Rites of Zhou fully sets forth the rules for laying out the capital and demarcating the countryside, and the principles for establishing offices and allocating duties. Truly, it is the Duke of Zhou’s book for bringing about Great Peace! Why, then, when its system of establishing fiefs does not agree with the “Royal Regulations,” and its system for establishing a capital does not agree with the “Announcement concerning Luo,” do people say, “This is a book about King Wen’s government of Qi, a book about the management of finances at Chengzhou”? When they see that its system of nine territorial zones does not agree with the “Tribute of Yu,” and its system of six ministries does not agree with the “Offices of Zhou,” they say, “This is a book of secret schemes from the Warring States period, a book of strained constructions by Han scholars.” How utterly thoughtless! By the time Liu Xin supplemented it with the Record of Artificers, matters had become impossible to investigate conclusively, and the Offices of Winter appeared to have been lost. Thus earlier scholars said that the sages’ Classics…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
不亡於秦火而壞於漢儒若内史司士之
類當屬之天官大司樂之類當屬之地官
春官之文有雜在他官者如封人大小行
人之類是也夏官之文有雜在他官者如
銜枚氏司隷之類是也掌祭之類知其非
秋官之文縣師廛人之類知其為冬官之
文長必有屬屬必以隷長緣職掌以考之
參文義以稽之則冬官固未嘗缺也明矣
此非吳文正公之意也陳氏俞氏之意也
===
古者述朝享聘祭之儀車旗服飾之制謂
之曰儀禮孔門弟子述其古禮之遺變禮
之由謂之曰曲禮夫固先王經世之典也
奈之何議儀禮者則曰馬鄭敘述周禮而
不及儀禮劉班敘述儀文而不及儀禮喪
服皆講師問荅之語終篇無天子諸侯之
文其議禮記者則曰曲禮作于曲臺王制
成于博士月令記秦世之官緇衣非魯論
之舊吁亦何不思之甚哉及至王安石參
punctuated:
不亡於秦火，而壞於漢儒。若内史、司士之類，當屬之天官；大司樂之類，當屬之地官。春官之文有雜在他官者，如封人、大小行人之類是也；夏官之文有雜在他官者，如銜枚氏、司隷之類是也。掌祭之類，知其非秋官之文；縣師、廛人之類，知其為冬官之文。長必有屬，屬必以隷長。緣職掌以考之，參文義以稽之，則冬官固未嘗缺也，明矣。此非吳文正公之意也，陳氏、俞氏之意也。

古者述朝享聘祭之儀、車旗服飾之制，謂之曰《儀禮》。孔門弟子述其古禮之遺、變禮之由，謂之曰《曲禮》。夫固先王經世之典也，奈之何議《儀禮》者則曰：「馬、鄭敘述《周禮》而不及《儀禮》，劉、班敘述儀文而不及《儀禮》。《喪服》皆講師問荅之語，終篇無天子諸侯之文。」其議《禮記》者則曰：「《曲禮》作于曲臺，《王制》成于博士，《月令》記秦世之官，《緇衣》非《魯論》之舊。」吁，亦何不思之甚哉！及至王安石參
translation_en:
…were not lost in the fires of Qin, but were corrupted by Han scholars. Offices such as the Palace Secretary and the Director of Officials ought to belong to the Ministry of Heaven; offices such as the Music Master-in-Chief ought to belong to the Ministry of Earth. Some passages belonging to the Ministry of Spring are interspersed among those of other ministries, as with the Boundary Officer and the Senior and Junior Messengers. Some passages belonging to the Ministry of Summer are interspersed among those of other ministries, as with the Officer of Gags and the Director of Bondservants. Offices such as the Director of Sacrifices [?] can be recognized as not belonging to the text of the Ministry of Autumn; offices such as the District Supervisor and the Market-Shop Officer can be recognized as belonging to the text of the Ministry of Winter. Every superior must have subordinates, and every subordinate must be subject to a superior. If we examine the offices according to their responsibilities and check them against the wording and meaning of the text, it becomes clear that the Ministry of Winter was never actually missing. This is not the interpretation of Wu Wenzheng alone, but also that of Master Chen and Master Yu.

In antiquity, accounts of the ceremonies for court audiences, offerings, diplomatic visits, and sacrifices, and of the regulations for carriages, banners, clothing, and ornaments, were called the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili). The disciples of Confucius recorded the surviving ancient rites and the reasons for changes in ritual; this was called the Summary of Rites (Quli). These were indeed the canonical rules by which the former kings ordered the world. Why, then, do critics of the Ceremonies and Rites say: “Ma and Zheng expounded the Rites of Zhou but did not discuss the Ceremonies and Rites; Liu and Ban described ritual forms but did not discuss the Ceremonies and Rites. The Mourning Dress chapter consists entirely of questions and answers from teachers, and throughout the chapter there is no text concerning the Son of Heaven or the feudal lords”? Those who criticize the Record of Rites (Liji) say: “The Summary of Rites was composed at the Qu Terrace; the Royal Regulations was produced by erudites; the Monthly Ordinances records offices of the Qin period; and the Black Robes does not preserve the old text of the Lu Analects.” Alas, how utterly thoughtless this is! Then, when Wang Anshi brought into comparison …

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以新經義遂至不列學官而此書遂廢矣
故愚謂聖經既壞於漢儒復大壞於宋相
若儀禮有冠禮有昏禮禮記則有冠義昏
義儀禮有士相見禮有鄉飲酒禮禮記則
有士相見義鄉飲酒義儀禮有鄉射禮有
大射禮禮記則有鄉射義大射義儀禮有
燕禮有聘禮禮記則有燕義聘義禮必有
義義以釋禮緣文義以考之參經籍以證
之則禮記非自爲經明矣此非吳文正公
===
之意也考亭夫子之意也然說周禮者有
謂九嬪九御何以雜乎天官庖人饔人何
以勞乎冢宰宗伯典禮文矣而遺於教司
馬專賦稅矣而兼乎兵其他絲人司裘近
乎奢貫齒塞淵近乎誣灑灰殺黽近於慘
置官之可疑已如是矣抑不知周公大小
相維之深意乎讀儀禮有謂古禮五十七
篇今而冠公符於首則是分飲射爲二則
非置投壺於末則是分器運爲二則非篇
punctuated:
以新經義，遂至不列學官，而此書遂廢矣。故愚謂聖經既壞於漢儒，復大壞於宋相。若《儀禮》有冠禮，有昏禮，《禮記》則有冠義、昏義；《儀禮》有士相見禮，有鄉飲酒禮，《禮記》則有士相見義、鄉飲酒義；《儀禮》有鄉射禮，有大射禮，《禮記》則有鄉射義、大射義；《儀禮》有燕禮，有聘禮，《禮記》則有燕義、聘義。禮必有義，義以釋禮。緣文義以考之，參經籍以證之，則《禮記》非自爲經明矣。此非吳文正公之意也，考亭夫子之意也。
然說《周禮》者，有謂：「九嬪、九御，何以雜乎天官？庖人、饔人，何以勞乎冢宰？宗伯典禮文矣，而遺於教；司馬專賦稅矣，而兼乎兵。其他絲人、司裘，近乎奢；貫齒、塞淵，近乎誣；灑灰、殺黽，近於慘。置官之可疑，已如是矣。」抑不知周公大小相維之深意乎？讀《儀禮》，有謂：「古禮五十七篇，今而冠公符於首則是，分飲射爲二則非；置投壺於末則是，分器運爲二則非。」篇
translation_en:
…with the New Interpretations of the Classics, ultimately causing it to be excluded from the curriculum of the official schools; thus this book fell into disuse. Hence, in my humble opinion, the sages’ classics, already damaged by Han Confucians, were damaged still more gravely by the Song chief councillor.
For example, the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) contains the capping and marriage rites, while the Record of Rites (Liji) contains explanations of the meaning of capping and marriage. The Ceremonies and Rites contains the rites for officers meeting one another and for district wine drinking, while the Record of Rites contains explanations of their meaning. The Ceremonies and Rites contains the district archery and great archery rites, while the Record of Rites contains explanations of their meaning. The Ceremonies and Rites contains the rites for banquets and diplomatic visits, while the Record of Rites contains explanations of their meaning. Rites necessarily have meaning, and explanations of meaning elucidate the rites. If we examine the wording and meaning and consult the canonical writings for corroboration, it becomes clear that the Record of Rites is not a self-standing classic. This is not merely the opinion of Lord Wu Wenzheng; it is the opinion of the Master of Kaoting, Zhu Xi.
Yet some who discuss the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) say: “Why are the Nine Concubines and Nine Attendants [?] intermingled with the Offices of Heaven? Why should the cooks and food preparers burden the Minister of State? The Minister of Rites administers ritual observances but neglects instruction; the Minister of War specializes in levies and taxes yet also takes charge of military affairs. Other offices, such as those responsible for silk and fur garments, verge on extravagance. Stringing teeth and blocking deep pools [?] verge on deception; scattering ashes and killing frogs verge on cruelty. Such are already the grounds for doubting the establishment of these offices.” Do they not understand the Duke of Zhou’s profound intention that the greater and lesser offices should sustain one another?
Some who read the Ceremonies and Rites say: “The ancient rites comprised fifty-seven chapters. In the present arrangement, placing ‘Gongfu’ first [?] is correct, but separating wine drinking and archery into two chapters is wrong. Placing Pitch-pot last is correct, but separating ‘Vessels’ and ‘Evolution’ into two chapters [?] is wrong.” As for the chapters…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
目增損之可疑又如是矣抑不知二戴之
去留固非而飲射諸篇之不可合者固也
必欲足古目之數析文義之同而章句之
間有不能强通者矣惡乎貴哉嗟夫周禮
果可行於今乎曰奚為而不可行焉匪周
禮宜惟人無弊不行焉惟人之弊匪周禮
弗宜既昔周公未作之時思兼三王以仰
思四事固不獨求三王之迹也欲師周公
者其不合者亦仰而思之耳若一一按其
===
迹而行之則古今異宜彼此異勢此新莽
所以敗於前而神宗又敗於後乎或謂王
通如用周禮其行乎愚曰幸王通之未用
耳使通而見用則人見周公而戚嗤矣夫
王通之學夫子不以其道而拘拘於言語
文字之間其能會周公之意於千載之上
乎夫明以達道道以會禮禮以察物物以
經政政以是則周公之意得矣故曰天下
之禍莫大於悖古亦莫大於泥古謹對
punctuated:
目增損之可疑又如是矣，抑不知二戴之去留固非，而飲射諸篇之不可合者固也。必欲足古目之數，析文義之同，而章句之間有不能强通者矣，惡乎貴哉？
嗟夫！周禮果可行於今乎？曰：奚為而不可行焉？匪周禮宜，惟人無弊不行焉；惟人之弊，匪周禮弗宜。既昔周公未作之時，思兼三王以仰思四事，固不獨求三王之迹也。欲師周公者，其不合者亦仰而思之耳。若一一按其迹而行之，則古今異宜，彼此異勢，此新莽所以敗於前而神宗又敗於後乎？或謂王通如用周禮，其行乎？愚曰：幸王通之未用耳！使通而見用，則人見周公而戚嗤矣。夫王通之學夫子，不以其道，而拘拘於言語文字之間，其能會周公之意於千載之上乎？夫明以達道，道以會禮，禮以察物，物以經政，政以是，則周公之意得矣。故曰：天下之禍，莫大於悖古，亦莫大於泥古。謹對。
translation_en:
…The additions to and deletions from the list of chapters are likewise open to doubt. Yet does this not overlook the fact that, although the two Dai scholars’ decisions about what to retain and discard were indeed mistaken, the chapters on drinking and archery certainly cannot be combined? If one insists on making up the number in the ancient list and splitting passages with the same meaning, there will be places among the chapters and sentences whose coherence cannot be forced. What value is there in that?
Alas! Can the Rites of Zhou really be put into practice today? I reply: why should they not be practicable? Whether the Rites of Zhou are appropriate depends on people; without failings, they would not go unpracticed [?]. It is people who are at fault, not the Rites of Zhou that are unsuitable. In former times, before the Duke of Zhou undertook his work, he considered drawing together the practices of the Three Kings and looking upward to ponder the four matters [?]; he certainly did not seek merely the outward traces of the Three Kings’ practices. Those who wish to take the Duke of Zhou as their teacher should likewise look upward and reflect upon whatever does not fit. If they follow his outward practices one by one, circumstances call for different arrangements in antiquity and today, and conditions differ from place to place. Is this not why Wang Mang of the Xin dynasty failed earlier, and Emperor Shenzong failed later?
Someone asks: if Wang Tong had employed the Rites of Zhou, would they have worked? In my humble opinion, it was fortunate that Wang Tong was never employed! Had he been employed, people would have regarded the Duke of Zhou with dismay and derision [?]. In emulating Confucius, Wang Tong did not follow his Way but confined himself narrowly to words and writings. How could he have grasped the intentions of the Duke of Zhou, who lived more than a thousand years before him? Through understanding, one apprehends the Way; through the Way, one comprehends ritual; through ritual, one examines things; through things, one orders government; and government thereby becomes correct. Then the Duke of Zhou’s intentions are grasped. Thus it is said: among the calamities of the world, none is greater than repudiating antiquity, and none is greater than clinging rigidly to antiquity. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第三問
周采
同考試官訓導余批自樂經既亡此學失
傳久矣有宋諸大儒繼作始有定論吾子敷對
詳明鑿鑿可據讀之使人忘倦真所謂善待問者
同考試官教諭周批問樂一策經生能得
肯綮者甚少此作長於考據蓋其用心之日久
矣健羨健羨
考試官主事吳批求元聲以復古樂此今日要
===
務知樂如子者可以薦矣
考試官郎中郭批不泛不略
欲求聖人作樂之妙當先求之作樂之本
次求之作樂之文蓋聖人之樂有本有文
本者其體也文者其用也非體不立非用
不行體者何聲氣之元是也用者何律呂
之具是也因聲氣以定律呂因律呂以和
聲氣此二者交相爲用而不可偏廢者然
於先後之間當知其序庶乎樂之妙可求
punctuated:
第三問
周采
同考試官訓導余批：「自樂經既亡，此學失傳久矣。有宋諸大儒繼作，始有定論。吾子敷對詳明，鑿鑿可據，讀之使人忘倦，真所謂善待問者。」
同考試官教諭周批：「問樂一策，經生能得肯綮者甚少。此作長於考據，蓋其用心之日久矣。健羨！健羨！」
考試官主事吳批：「求元聲以復古樂，此今日要務。知樂如子者，可以薦矣。」
考試官郎中郭批：「不泛不略。」
欲求聖人作樂之妙，當先求之作樂之本，次求之作樂之文。蓋聖人之樂有本有文，本者其體也，文者其用也。非體不立，非用不行。體者何？聲氣之元是也。用者何？律呂之具是也。因聲氣以定律呂，因律呂以和聲氣，此二者交相爲用而不可偏廢者。然於先後之間當知其序，庶乎樂之妙可求
translation_en:
Third Question
Zhou Cai

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: “Since the loss of the Classic of Music, this learning has long lacked transmission. Only when the great Confucian scholars of the Song arose in succession were settled conclusions reached. Your response expounds the subject clearly and fully, with firm grounds for its claims. Reading it makes one forget fatigue. You truly deserve to be called adept at answering questions.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “On this policy question concerning music, very few students of the classics can grasp the crux. This composition excels in its examination of textual evidence; surely its author has devoted himself to the subject for a long time. How admirable! How admirable!”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Secretary: “Seeking the fundamental tone in order to restore ancient music is an essential task today. Someone with your understanding of music may indeed be recommended.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Director: “Neither diffuse nor cursory.”

To seek the subtle mastery with which the sages created music, one must first investigate the foundation of their music-making, and then its patterned expression. For the sages’ music has both a foundation and a patterned expression: the foundation is its substance, and the patterned expression is its function. Without substance it cannot be established; without function it cannot operate. What is its substance? The primal source of sound and vital breath. What is its function? The apparatus of the pitch standards, lü and lü. Sound and vital breath provide the basis for determining the pitch standards; the pitch standards provide the basis for harmonizing sound and vital breath. These two serve one another, and neither may be neglected. Yet one must understand their proper sequence of precedence, so that the subtle mastery of music may be sought…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
矣柰何世之言樂者不求之金石之錙銖
則求之秬黍之毫末嗚呼其於樂也淺矣
安得知樂者而與之言樂哉此三代而下
愚深有取程張朱蔡之論而不徒於律呂
金石之間已也敢以是爲明問復夫自黃
帝堯舜皆以功成而作樂其曰雲門言衆
和之所出也其曰咸池言無不被也其曰
韶謂其紹聖人之後也曰大濩非謂其能
救民乎曰大武非謂其能止戈乎是其樂
===
也既非無因而强作而其作也又得夫聲
氣之元此其志氣天人交相感應不呂而
和不律而節論倫無患樂之情也欣喜歡
愛樂之官也執事所謂獨得創作之妙者
非與易曰雷出地奮豫先王以作樂崇德
書曰詩言志歌永言聲依永律和聲既象
其聲復取其義聲所由生聲所由和執事
所謂論樂之始者非與天地之數始於一
終於十一三五七九爲陽九者陽之成也
punctuated:
矣。柰何世之言樂者，不求之金石之錙銖，則求之秬黍之毫末。嗚呼！其於樂也淺矣！安得知樂者而與之言樂哉？此三代而下，愚深有取程張朱蔡之論，而不徒於律呂金石之間已也。敢以是爲明問復。
夫自黃帝堯舜，皆以功成而作樂。其曰雲門，言衆和之所出也；其曰咸池，言無不被也；其曰韶，謂其紹聖人之後也；曰大濩，非謂其能救民乎？曰大武，非謂其能止戈乎？是其樂也，既非無因而强作，而其作也，又得夫聲氣之元。此其志氣天人交相感應，不呂而和，不律而節。論倫無患，樂之情也；欣喜歡愛，樂之官也。執事所謂獨得創作之妙者，非與？《易》曰：「雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德。」《書》曰：「詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。」既象其聲，復取其義。聲所由生，聲所由和，執事所謂論樂之始者，非與？天地之數，始於一，終於十。一三五七九爲陽，九者陽之成也。
translation_en:
…may thus be sought. Yet why do those of our age who discuss music seek it either in the minute weights of bells and stone chimes or in the tiniest measurements of black millet grains? Alas, how shallow their understanding of music is! Where might I find someone who understands music, with whom I could discuss it? Thus, among the discussions since the Three Dynasties, I, in my ignorance, find much to approve in those of Cheng, Zhang, Zhu, and Cai, rather than confining myself merely to pitch standards, bells, and stone chimes. I venture to offer this in reply to your illuminating question.
From Huangdi, Yao, and Shun onward, rulers all created music upon completing their achievements. The name Cloud Gate (Yunmen) signifies the source from which all harmonies emerge; All-Pervading Pool (Xianchi) signifies that nothing is untouched by its influence; Succession (Shao) signifies carrying on the succession of the sages. As for Great Deliverance (Dahu), does its name not signify the ability to save the people? As for Great Martial Achievement (Dawu), does its name not signify the ability to halt warfare? Their music was therefore not arbitrarily created without a basis; in creating it, they also grasped the source of sound and vital energy. Thus their intentions and vital energies, and Heaven and humanity, responded reciprocally to one another: harmony arose without the lü pitch standards, and measured order without the律 pitch standards. Ordered relationships free from trouble [?] are the essential feeling of music; delight, joy, gladness, and affection are its functions. Is this not what you call their unique mastery of the subtle art of musical creation?
The Book of Changes says: “Thunder emerges from the earth and stirs: Enthusiasm. The former kings accordingly made music to exalt virtue.” The Book of Documents says: “Poetry expresses intention; song prolongs words; musical tones follow the prolonged utterance; pitch standards harmonize the tones.” They both imitated its sounds and drew upon its meaning. The source from which sound arises and the means by which sound is harmonized—is this not what you mean by discussing the beginnings of music? The numbers of Heaven and Earth begin with one and end with ten. One, three, five, seven, and nine are yang; nine is the culmination of yang.

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
二四六八十爲陰十者陰之成也陽聲之
始陽氣之動均其長得九寸審其圍則九
分此十二律以黄鍾爲重宫最大而沉濁
羽最細而輕清商之大次宫徵之細次羽
而角居四者之中然世之論中不以角而
以宫盖聲陽也自下而上未及其半則属
於陰而未暢故不可用上而及半然後属
於陽而始和故即其始而用之以爲宫之
一聲正當眾聲和與未和陰陽際會之中
===
此五音所以以宫爲主也八音之序先於
金石金石土爲陰陰逆推其所始是以先
金石而後土匏竹木爲陽陽順序其所生
是以先匏竹而後木革絲居陰陽之正是
以先革而後絲二音之變獨於宫徵者宫
與商商與角徵與羽相去皆一律角與徵
羽與宫相去皆二律一律則近而和二律
則遠而不相及故宫羽之間有變宫角徵
之間有變徵此皆出於自然以濟五聲之
punctuated: 二四六八十爲陰，十者陰之成也。陽聲之始，陽氣之動，均其長得九寸，審其圍則九分。此十二律以黄鍾爲重。宫最大而沉濁，羽最細而輕清，商之大次宫，徵之細次羽，而角居四者之中。然世之論中，不以角而以宫。盖聲陽也，自下而上，未及其半則属於陰而未暢，故不可用；上而及半，然後属於陽而始和，故即其始而用之，以爲宫之一聲，正當眾聲和與未和、陰陽際會之中。此五音所以以宫爲主也。八音之序先於金石，金石土爲陰，陰逆推其所始，是以先金石而後土；匏竹木爲陽，陽順序其所生，是以先匏竹而後木；革絲居陰陽之正，是以先革而後絲。二音之變獨於宫徵者，宫與商、商與角、徵與羽，相去皆一律；角與徵、羽與宫，相去皆二律。一律則近而和，二律則遠而不相及，故宫羽之間有變宫，角徵之間有變徵。此皆出於自然，以濟五聲之
translation_en:
…Two, four, six, eight, and ten are yin; ten is the completion of yin. At the inception of yang sound, when yang qi begins to move, the calibrated length is nine cun, and the measured circumference is nine fen. Thus, among the twelve pitch standards, Huangzhong holds preeminence. Gong is the fullest tone, deep and weighty; yu is the thinnest, light and clear. Shang comes next to gong in fullness, and zhi comes next to yu in thinness, while jue occupies the middle among these four. Yet when people discuss the central tone, they take it to be gong rather than jue. This is because sound is yang: as it rises from below, before reaching the halfway point it belongs to yin and has not yet attained free expression, so it cannot be used. Only when it rises to the halfway point does it belong to yang and begin to harmonize. Thus this starting point is adopted as the tone gong, precisely at the center where the sounds pass from disharmony to harmony and where yin and yang meet. This is why gong governs the five tones.

In the ordering of the eight classes of musical instruments, metal and stone come first. Metal, stone, and earth belong to yin; yin is traced backward to its beginning, so metal and stone precede earth. Gourd, bamboo, and wood belong to yang; yang follows the forward sequence of generation, so gourd and bamboo precede wood. Hide and silk occupy the cardinal positions of yin and yang, so hide precedes silk. The reason the two altered tones occur only at gong and zhi is that gong and shang, shang and jue, and zhi and yu are each separated by one pitch standard, while jue and zhi, and yu and gong, are each separated by two pitch standards. An interval of one pitch standard is close and harmonious; an interval of two is distant, and the tones fail to connect. Thus between gong and yu there is altered gong, and between jue and zhi there is altered zhi. All this arises naturally, to make up for the five tones’…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
不及奈何聖遠道湮代更樂壞逮於東漢
之下以接西晋之初歷魏周齊隋唐五季
論者愈多而法愈不定及宋而胡阮李范
諸賢終不能以相一也執事欲復古樂而
以四子之說爲問生以用四子之說而古
樂庶可復也故必先求之作樂之本如周
子之復古禮以變今樂程子之考音聲以
定秬黍張子則以人之德性爲本蔡子則
先求聲氣之元庶乎元氣可求中聲可得
===
也如荀勗得牛鐸於趙人而聲律以諧故
當時有暗解之譽阮咸得玉尺於田夫而
較量無異故當時有神解之稱者然徒區
區於器數之末本則未知也次求之作樂
之文考漢斛之積分以定黃鍾圍徑之法
稽小司馬之說以定寸以九分之則五聲
二變之數變律半聲之例則杜氏之通典
具焉變宮變徵之不得爲調則孔氏之禮
疏因亦可見庶乎吹之則聲和候之則氣
punctuated:
不及。奈何聖遠道湮，代更樂壞，逮於東漢之下，以接西晋之初，歷魏、周、齊、隋、唐、五季，論者愈多而法愈不定。及宋，而胡、阮、李、范諸賢終不能以相一也。執事欲復古樂，而以四子之說爲問，生以用四子之說，而古樂庶可復也。故必先求之作樂之本：如周子之復古禮以變今樂，程子之考音聲以定秬黍，張子則以人之德性爲本，蔡子則先求聲氣之元，庶乎元氣可求，中聲可得也。如荀勗得牛鐸於趙人而聲律以諧，故當時有暗解之譽；阮咸得玉尺於田夫而較量無異，故當時有神解之稱者。然徒區區於器數之末，本則未知也。

次求之作樂之文：考漢斛之積分，以定黃鍾圍徑之法；稽小司馬之說，以定寸以九分之則。五聲二變之數、變律半聲之例，則杜氏之《通典》具焉；變宮、變徵之不得爲調，則孔氏之《禮疏》因亦可見。庶乎吹之則聲和，候之則氣
translation_en:
…to remedy what the five tones lack. Yet as the sages grew distant and the Way fell into obscurity, dynasties changed and music deteriorated. From the latter Eastern Han into the beginning of the Western Jin, and through Wei, Zhou, Qi, Sui, Tang, and the Five Dynasties, those discussing music became ever more numerous, while its methods became ever less settled. Even in the Song, the worthies Hu, Ruan, Li, and Fan ultimately could not reach agreement. You, honored examiners, wish to restore ancient music and have posed a question concerning the teachings of the four masters. This student believes that by applying their teachings, ancient music might indeed be restored. We must therefore first seek the foundations of making music. Master Zhou would restore ancient ritual to transform present-day music; Master Cheng would examine sounds to establish the standards of black millet used in measurement; Master Zhang took human moral nature as the foundation; and Master Cai first sought the source of sound and vital energy, qi. In this way, primordial qi might be sought out and the balanced tone attained. For example, Xun Xu obtained an ox bell from a man of Zhao and thereby brought the pitches into harmony, earning contemporary praise for intuitive understanding. Ruan Xian obtained a jade ruler from a farmer, and comparison revealed no discrepancy, earning contemporary acclaim for inspired understanding. Yet these achievements merely concerned the subsidiary matters of instruments and numerical measures; the foundations remained unknown.

Next, we must investigate the formal particulars of making music. We should examine the calculated volume of the Han hu measure to establish the method for determining the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong, or Yellow Bell, pitch pipe; and consult the explanation of the Younger Sima to establish the rule of nine fen to one cun. The numerical relations of the five tones and two altered tones, and the rules for altered pitches and half-length pitches, are fully set out in Master Du’s Comprehensive Institutions. That the altered gong and altered zhi tones cannot serve as the basis of a mode can also be seen in Master Kong’s Commentary on the Rites [the connecting wording is doubtful]. Thus, when the pipes are blown, their sounds might harmonize, and when used to observe seasonal influences, the qi might…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
應如王朴之所定以鍾律爲本范鎭之所
論以秬黍爲則然徒區區於文爲之具本
固未論也古樂何望哉嗟夫周衰樂廢典
籍不存後之言樂者拘夫器數之末雜以
鄭衛之音漢有宗廟樂有房中樂唐有凱
樂有燕樂宋有雅樂有平晉樂有朝天樂
不過助慾長怨何能有補哉然樂之制雖
亡而樂之本尚在盖和樂者樂之本也學
者誠能和樂以養其心而樂之本庶其在
===
是乎執事以爲何如耶
第四問
胡彥
同考試官教諭陳 批 刑之爲用固不可廢
尤有不可不慎者此策稽經證史雖舉寛嚴並
論而必以矜恤爲主藹然長厚之意溢於言表
可以占其所存矣
同考試官學正陳 批 刑罰之道本諸仁義
隨其所感而順應之耳觀其所對具得此意盖
punctuated:
應。如王朴之所定，以鍾律爲本；范鎭之所論，以秬黍爲則。然徒區區於文爲之具，本固未論也，古樂何望哉！嗟夫！周衰樂廢，典籍不存，後之言樂者拘夫器數之末，雜以鄭衛之音。漢有宗廟樂，有房中樂；唐有凱樂，有燕樂；宋有雅樂，有平晉樂，有朝天樂。不過助慾長怨，何能有補哉！然樂之制雖亡，而樂之本尚在。盖和樂者，樂之本也。學者誠能和樂以養其心，而樂之本庶其在是乎！執事以爲何如耶？

第四問
胡彥

同考試官教諭陳批：刑之爲用，固不可廢，尤有不可不慎者。此策稽經證史，雖舉寛嚴並論，而必以矜恤爲主，藹然長厚之意溢於言表，可以占其所存矣。

同考試官學正陳批：刑罰之道，本諸仁義，隨其所感而順應之耳。觀其所對，具得此意，盖
translation_en:
…responds. Wang Pu’s determinations took the pitch standards of bells as their basis; Fan Zhen’s arguments took black millet grains as their measure. Yet they merely busied themselves with the apparatus of formal practice, leaving the root unexamined. What hope, then, was there of recovering ancient music? Alas! As the Zhou declined, music fell into disuse, and its canonical writings did not survive. Those who subsequently discussed music were confined to the incidental details of instruments and numerical measures, mingling them with the sounds of Zheng and Wei. The Han had ancestral-temple music and music of the inner chambers; the Tang had victory music and banquet music; the Song had elegant music, music for the Pacification of Jin, and music for Attendance at Heaven’s Court. These merely encouraged desire and fostered resentment: how could they offer any benefit? Yet although the institutions of music have vanished, its root remains. Harmony and joy are the root of music. If students can truly nurture their hearts through harmony and joy, might not the root of music be found here? What is your judgment, honored examiner?

Fourth Question
Hu Yan

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor (jiaoyu): Punishment certainly cannot be dispensed with, but its use especially demands caution. This policy essay examines the classics and adduces historical evidence. Although it discusses leniency and severity together, it consistently makes compassion and solicitude its guiding principle. A warm spirit of generosity and kindness shines through its words, allowing us to discern what the author holds in his heart.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor (xuezheng): The proper way of punishment is rooted in benevolence and righteousness; it simply responds fittingly to the circumstances that call it forth. Examining his answer, we see that he has fully grasped this meaning. Indeed, …

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
知要領者
考試官主事吳批條荅不遺非淺學可到
考試官郎中郭批明贍
君子之用刑也寬而不失於縱嚴而不至
於殘夫用刑之道寬與嚴耳寬以濟嚴之
太過嚴以損寬之有餘則刑罰中而民服
矣或主於寬寬則民慢而惠奸長惡之風
不可禁也或主於嚴嚴則民殘而草薙禽
獮之慘豈不良可憫哉故寬可也一於寬
===
則不可也一於寬不可也一於嚴尤不可
也不一於嚴則嚴未嘗不寬不一於寬則
寬未嘗不嚴寬嚴相濟刑斯理矣執事以
寬猛之宜下詢承學其意不在茲與愚也
敢以是為明問復天生五材孰能去兵聖
人五教孰能去刑刑之說何自而始乎易
曰利用刑人又曰利用獄曰先王以明罰
勑法曰君子以折獄致刑書曰五刑有服
五服三就曰上刑適輕下服下刑適重上
punctuated:
知要領者。
考試官主事吳批：條荅不遺，非淺學可到。
考試官郎中郭批：明贍。
君子之用刑也，寬而不失於縱，嚴而不至於殘。夫用刑之道，寬與嚴耳。寬以濟嚴之太過，嚴以損寬之有餘，則刑罰中而民服矣。或主於寬，寬則民慢，而惠奸長惡之風不可禁也；或主於嚴，嚴則民殘，而草薙禽獮之慘，豈不良可憫哉？故寬可也，一於寬則不可也。一於寬不可也，一於嚴尤不可也。不一於嚴，則嚴未嘗不寬；不一於寬，則寬未嘗不嚴。寬嚴相濟，刑斯理矣。執事以寬猛之宜下詢承學，其意不在茲與？愚也敢以是為明問復。
天生五材，孰能去兵？聖人五教，孰能去刑？刑之說何自而始乎？《易》曰：「利用刑人。」又曰：「利用獄。」曰：「先王以明罰勑法。」曰：「君子以折獄致刑。」《書》曰：「五刑有服，五服三就。」曰：「上刑適輕下服，下刑適重上
translation_en:
…one who understands the essentials.
Examiner Wu, a Secretary, comments: “His answers address each point without omission. This is beyond the reach of shallow learning.”
Examiner Guo, a Director, comments: “Clear and ample.”
When the gentleman employs punishment, he is lenient without lapsing into indulgence and strict without descending into cruelty. The way of employing punishment consists simply in leniency and strictness. Leniency corrects excessive strictness, and strictness curbs excessive leniency; punishments then strike the proper balance, and the people submit. Some make leniency their guiding principle; yet leniency makes the people heedless, and the tendency to favor the wicked and foster evil becomes impossible to restrain. Others make strictness their guiding principle; yet strictness brings suffering upon the people. Is not the cruelty of cutting them down like grass and slaughtering them like hunted animals truly pitiable? Thus leniency is permissible, but exclusive reliance upon leniency is not. If exclusive reliance upon leniency is unacceptable, exclusive reliance upon strictness is still less acceptable. When strictness is not exclusive, it never lacks leniency; when leniency is not exclusive, it never lacks strictness. When leniency and strictness temper one another, punishment is properly administered. You, honored examiners, have deigned to ask us students about the proper use of leniency and severity: is this not what you intend? I, in my ignorance, venture to offer this in reply to your illuminating question.
Heaven produced the five materials: who can dispense with arms? The sages established the five teachings: who can dispense with punishment? Where did the discourse on punishment originate? The Book of Changes says, “It is beneficial to punish people.” It also says, “It is beneficial to employ judicial proceedings”; “The former kings clarified punishments and made the laws firm”; and “The gentleman adjudicates cases and carries out punishments.” The Book of Documents says, “The five punishments have their applications, and these five are carried out in three places.” It also says, “When an offense subject to a higher punishment warrants mitigation, apply the lower; when an offense subject to a lower punishment warrants aggravation, the higher…”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
服小司寇一曰詞聽二曰色聽三曰氣聽
四曰耳聽五曰目聽則刑固聖人之所不
免也曰罪疑惟輕曰辟以止辟曰君子以
議獄緩死曰君子以赦過宥罪曰聽獄訟
求民情曰原父子之親立君臣之義其微
意所在何甞不主於寬乎大舜之制刑曰
欽曰恤欽則恭承民命恤則視民如傷文
王之慎罰曰敬曰忌敬則有所不忽忌則
有所不敢故程子不取刻核之論謂嚴而
===
不求其情而其流必入於酷朱子獨憫死
者之無辜謂寬而失於縱則非所以爲寬
二子主寬之意將無同與漢之法始定於
蕭何中紛更於張湯桑弘羊再論於仲長
統崔寔其近於寬者惟文帝乎故志曰躬
脩玄默勸課農桑禁網疎闊斷獄四百唐
之法始議於長孫無忌戴冑中變於來俊
臣李林甫得其平者其高祖太宗乎故志
曰受隋禪而命劉文靜定律令之制以寬
punctuated:
服。《小司寇》：「一曰詞聽，二曰色聽，三曰氣聽，四曰耳聽，五曰目聽。」則刑固聖人之所不免也。曰「罪疑惟輕」，曰「辟以止辟」，曰「君子以議獄緩死」，曰「君子以赦過宥罪」，曰「聽獄訟，求民情」，曰「原父子之親，立君臣之義」，其微意所在，何甞不主於寬乎？大舜之制刑，曰欽，曰恤；欽則恭承民命，恤則視民如傷。文王之慎罰，曰敬，曰忌；敬則有所不忽，忌則有所不敢。故程子不取刻核之論，謂嚴而不求其情，而其流必入於酷。朱子獨憫死者之無辜，謂寬而失於縱，則非所以爲寬。二子主寬之意，將無同與？

漢之法，始定於蕭何，中紛更於張湯、桑弘羊，再論於仲長統、崔寔。其近於寬者，惟文帝乎？故志曰：「躬脩玄默，勸課農桑，禁網疎闊，斷獄四百。」唐之法，始議於長孫無忌、戴冑，中變於來俊臣、李林甫。得其平者，其高祖、太宗乎？故志曰：「受隋禪而命劉文靜定律令之制，以寬
translation_en:
…punishment. The “Lesser Minister of Justice” section states: “First, listen to their statements; second, observe their expressions; third, observe their breathing; fourth, observe their responses to what they hear; fifth, observe their eyes.” Thus even the sages could not dispense with punishments. Yet it is said, “When guilt is doubtful, choose the lighter punishment”; “Use punishment to put an end to punishment”; “The gentleman deliberates over judicial cases and delays executions”; “The gentleman pardons errors and mitigates offenses”; “In hearing lawsuits, seek the true circumstances of the people”; and “Trace matters back to the affection between father and son, and establish the righteousness between ruler and subject.” In their subtle intent, when have these teachings ever failed to favor leniency? In instituting punishments, the great Shun spoke of reverence and compassion. Reverence means treating the people's lives with respectful care; compassion means regarding the people as though they were suffering injury. In exercising caution over punishments, King Wen spoke of respect and apprehension. Respect means that there are matters one will not neglect; apprehension means that there are things one will not dare to do. Thus Master Cheng rejected arguments for harsh scrutiny, saying that severity without seeking the true circumstances must ultimately degenerate into cruelty. Master Zhu particularly pitied the innocent who were put to death, saying that leniency that lapses into indulgence is no way to practice leniency. Were the two masters not alike in their intention to favor leniency?

The laws of the Han were first established by Xiao He, repeatedly altered in the intervening period by Zhang Tang and Sang Hongyang, and discussed anew by Zhongchang Tong and Cui Shi. Was Emperor Wen alone in approaching leniency? Thus the historical treatise says: “He personally cultivated profound quietude, encouraged and supervised agriculture and sericulture, kept the net of prohibitions loose, and adjudicated four hundred criminal cases.” The laws of the Tang were first deliberated upon by Zhangsun Wuji and Dai Zhou, and altered in the intervening period by Lai Junchen and Li Linfu. Was it Gaozu and Taizong who achieved the proper balance? Thus the historical treatise says: “Upon receiving the throne through the Sui abdication, he ordered Liu Wenjing to establish the system of statutes and ordinances, using leniency…”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
仁而用魏徵行仁義之言宋祖以仁厚立
國以禮義爲治故志曰宋興削除苛暴委
任儒臣士初試官皆習律令一坐深文終
身不進其刑法之定於趙普諸賢則寛新
法之更於王安石則嚴中變於司馬光者
則寛繼變於秦檜者則嚴果可謂之純於
仁義乎刑之不得其平亦已久矣其間若
張釋之無冤民于定國之不冤暴勝之之
納諷徐有功之平恕求其善可爲法者非
===
斯人乎若商鞅之車裂張湯之自殺嚴延
年來俊臣輩之不得其死求其惡可爲戒
者又非斯人乎我
國家稽古定制律令有條不得以私情爲出
入頃歲以來
皇上有恤刑之
詔又命不必以成案爲因循其所以保邦本慎
國脉之意周且密矣今之司獄者將如何
而後可善乎張子之言曰治獄所以不得
punctuated:
仁，而用魏徵行仁義之言。宋祖以仁厚立國，以禮義爲治。故志曰：「宋興，削除苛暴，委任儒臣。士初試官，皆習律令，一坐深文，終身不進。」其刑法之定於趙普諸賢則寛，新法之更於王安石則嚴，中變於司馬光者則寛，繼變於秦檜者則嚴，果可謂之純於仁義乎？刑之不得其平，亦已久矣。其間若張釋之無冤民，于定國之不冤，暴勝之之納諷，徐有功之平恕，求其善可爲法者，非斯人乎？若商鞅之車裂，張湯之自殺，嚴延年、來俊臣輩之不得其死，求其惡可爲戒者，又非斯人乎？
我國家稽古定制，律令有條，不得以私情爲出入。頃歲以來，皇上有恤刑之詔，又命不必以成案爲因循。其所以保邦本、慎國脉之意，周且密矣。今之司獄者，將如何而後可善乎？張子之言曰：「治獄所以不得
translation_en:
…benevolence, and employed Wei Zheng, putting his counsel on benevolence and righteousness into practice. The founding emperor of the Song established the dynasty through benevolence and generosity, and governed through ritual propriety and righteousness. Thus the historical treatise states: “When the Song arose, it abolished harsh and oppressive practices and entrusted responsibilities to Confucian officials. All scholars entering their initial probationary appointments studied the statutes and ordinances. Anyone convicted even once of interpreting the law with undue severity was barred from advancement for life.” When Zhao Pu and the other worthy men established its penal laws, they were lenient; when Wang Anshi introduced the New Policies, they became severe. When Sima Guang subsequently changed them, they became lenient; when Qin Hui changed them in turn, they became severe. Can this truly be called an unalloyed commitment to benevolence and righteousness? Punishment has long failed to achieve fairness.
Among those of these times, Zhang Shizhi left no people unjustly treated; Yu Dingguo caused no wrongful convictions; Bao Shengzhi accepted admonition; and Xu Yougong was fair and forbearing. If we seek men whose good conduct can serve as a model, are these not the men? As for Shang Yang’s being torn apart by chariots, Zhang Tang’s suicide, and the violent deaths of men such as Yan Yannian and Lai Junchen: if we seek men whose evil conduct can serve as a warning, are these not also the men?
Our dynasty has examined antiquity and established its institutions. Its statutes and ordinances have clearly defined provisions, and private feelings must not determine whether someone is exempted from or subjected to punishment. In recent years, His Majesty has issued an edict calling for compassion in punishment, and has further ordered that established precedents need not be followed mechanically. His intention to preserve the foundations of the realm and safeguard the state’s lifeblood is comprehensive and meticulous indeed. How, then, should those responsible for judicial proceedings today act in order to discharge their duties well? Master Zhang said: “The reasons why the adjudication of cases fails to attain…”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其平者盖有數說視上官之趨向而重輕
其手惑胥吏之浮言而二三其心不盡其
情而一以威惕之不原其初而一以法繩
之西山真氏之誡同官曰斷獄不公聽訟
不審淹延囚繫慘酷用刑泛濫追呼招引
告訐吾何爲犯其議以虧皇天好生之德
乎嗚呼夫刑非得已而用之也以不得已
而用之則刑寛而民服以得已而用之則
刑酷而民寃故聖人之治尚德不尚刑聖
===
人之刑尚寛不尚嚴司刑者毋或得已而
不已也
第五問
陳錠
同考試官教諭黄 批 理財乃
今日之急務周禮寔理財之成法用觀士子才識以裨實用此
策援古證今論有根據且經畫利弊纖巨不遺
鑿鑿可施之用不意韋布中乃有留心天下如
此者
punctuated:
其平者，盖有數說：視上官之趨向而重輕其手，惑胥吏之浮言而二三其心，不盡其情而一以威惕之，不原其初而一以法繩之。」西山真氏之誡同官曰：「斷獄不公，聽訟不審，淹延囚繫，慘酷用刑，泛濫追呼，招引告訐，吾何爲犯其議以虧皇天好生之德乎？」嗚呼！夫刑非得已而用之也。以不得已而用之，則刑寛而民服；以得已而用之，則刑酷而民寃。故聖人之治尚德不尚刑，聖人之刑尚寛不尚嚴。司刑者毋或得已而不已也。

第五問
陳錠

同考試官教諭黄批：「理財乃今日之急務，《周禮》寔理財之成法，用觀士子才識，以裨實用。此策援古證今，論有根據，且經畫利弊，纖巨不遺，鑿鑿可施之用。不意韋布中乃有留心天下如此者
translation_en:
…their fairness, there are several explanations: those handling cases make their actions harsher or lighter according to their superiors’ inclinations; misled by the clerks’ unfounded talk, they waver in their judgment; without fully investigating the circumstances, they rely entirely on intimidation; and without tracing the matter to its beginnings, they rely entirely on the law to judge it.” Zhen Xishan admonished his fellow officials, saying: “To decide criminal cases unfairly, hear lawsuits without careful scrutiny, prolong imprisonment, inflict cruel punishments, issue indiscriminate summonses, and encourage accusatory denunciations—why should I incur such censure and impair August Heaven’s virtue of cherishing life?” Alas! Punishment is to be employed only when unavoidable. When employed because it is unavoidable, punishment is lenient and the people submit; when employed although it could be avoided, punishment is cruel and the people suffer injustice. Thus the sage’s government prizes virtue rather than punishment, and the sage’s punishments prize leniency rather than severity. Let those administering punishment never fail to desist when they can.

Fifth Question
Chen Ding

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Managing public finances is an urgent task today. The Rites of Zhou indeed provides established methods for financial administration; this question serves to reveal the candidates’ ability and discernment, so that these may contribute to practical affairs. This policy essay draws upon antiquity to substantiate its discussion of the present, and its arguments are well grounded. Moreover, in its planning it leaves out neither benefits nor drawbacks, whether small or great, offering concrete measures that can be implemented. I had not expected to find among commoner scholars someone who takes the affairs of the realm so much to heart…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
大庭之對吾於子不能無望矣
考試官主事吳批博洽之才經濟之學場中如
子者可多得耶
考試官郎中郭批區畫時務悉自胷中流出末
復歸重儉德可謂知本之論矣
國依於民則知民財之不可不足財蠹於
用則知國用之不可無經夫財出於民者
也而豐儉之度則制於君也使其取諸下
者無藝用于上者無節則上下俱困而國
===
非其國故八政以食貨爲先而庶矣必繼
以富此制治保邦之要道而聖君賢相不
可一日不講者也理財之法吾於成周得
其詳焉周禮一書周公致太平之典也而
理財之道大要有三生天下之財存乎仁
取天下之財存乎義用天下之財存乎禮
是故繫之九兩以定其業任之九職以厚
其生雖無常職者尤使之轉移執事仁以
生財之謂也財足矣然後制九府之法以
punctuated:
大庭之對，吾於子不能無望矣。
考試官主事吳批：博洽之才，經濟之學，場中如子者，可多得耶？
考試官郎中郭批：區畫時務，悉自胷中流出，末復歸重儉德，可謂知本之論矣。
國依於民，則知民財之不可不足；財蠹於用，則知國用之不可無經。夫財出於民者也，而豐儉之度則制於君也。使其取諸下者無藝，用于上者無節，則上下俱困，而國非其國。故八政以食貨爲先，而庶矣必繼以富。此制治保邦之要道，而聖君賢相不可一日不講者也。理財之法，吾於成周得其詳焉。《周禮》一書，周公致太平之典也，而理財之道大要有三：生天下之財存乎仁，取天下之財存乎義，用天下之財存乎禮。是故繫之九兩以定其業，任之九職以厚其生，雖無常職者，尤使之轉移執事，仁以生財之謂也。財足矣，然後制九府之法以
translation_en:
…As for your response at the imperial court, I cannot but place hopes in you.
Examiner Wu, Secretary, comments: With your wide-ranging talents and learning in statecraft, could many like you be found among the candidates here?
Examiner Guo, Director, comments: Your plans for the affairs of the day all flow from your own understanding. At the end, you again give foremost weight to the virtue of frugality. This may indeed be called an argument that understands the fundamentals.
Since the state depends upon the people, we know that the people’s resources must be sufficient; since expenditure consumes resources, we know that state spending must follow established principles. Wealth comes from the people, but the measure of lavishness or frugality is determined by the ruler. If what is taken from those below has no limit, and what is spent by those above has no restraint, then above and below alike will be impoverished, and the state will cease to be a state. Thus, among the eight concerns of government, food and goods come first; and once the people are numerous, making them prosperous must follow. This is the essential way to establish good government and preserve the realm, which sage rulers and worthy ministers must not neglect to consider for even a day.
I find the methods of managing wealth set out in detail in the institutions of the perfected Zhou. The Rites of Zhou is the canonical record of how the Duke of Zhou brought about great peace. Its way of managing wealth has three main principles: generating the wealth of the realm rests upon benevolence; collecting the wealth of the realm rests upon righteousness; and spending the wealth of the realm rests upon ritual propriety. Thus, the people were bound together through the nine bonds to give stability to their occupations, and assigned the nine categories of work to enrich their livelihoods. Even those without regular occupations were put to transporting goods and performing services. This is what is meant by generating wealth through benevolence. Once resources were sufficient, rules for the nine treasuries [?] were then established in order to…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
取之輕重多寡內外遠近皆酌爲中制而
無一毫之過焉義以取財之謂也而又制
爲九式之法以用之自祭祀賓客以至匪
頒好用從而均節之焉禮以用財之謂也
三者舉而理道得矣若王莽用之而敗於
前王安石用之而敗於後非周禮之罪也
用之者之罪也孔子曰若欲行而法則周
公之典在王通亦曰如有用我執此以往
舍周官而言經制者未見其爲可也賦役
===
繁重秦不足道也漢懲秦弊田租十五稅
一加以文帝之躬行節儉專務休息却駿
馬而不御罷露臺而不脩此其所以海內
富庶錢朽粟紅至於武帝之時內侈土木
外勤兵役海內虛耗則財惡得而不匱哉
賦役煩苛隋不足道也唐承隋後授人以
口分世業之田加以太宗之敦行仁義安
養困窮重民力而罷遠戍鑒秦失而停𠠎
村此其所以斗米三錢夜戶不閉至於天
punctuated:
取之，輕重多寡、內外遠近，皆酌爲中制，而無一毫之過焉，義以取財之謂也。而又制爲九式之法以用之，自祭祀賓客以至匪頒好用，從而均節之焉，禮以用財之謂也。三者舉，而理道得矣。若王莽用之而敗於前，王安石用之而敗於後，非周禮之罪也，用之者之罪也。孔子曰：「若欲行而法，則周公之典在。」王通亦曰：「如有用我，執此以往。」舍周官而言經制者，未見其爲可也。

賦役繁重，秦不足道也。漢懲秦弊，田租十五稅一，加以文帝之躬行節儉，專務休息，却駿馬而不御，罷露臺而不脩，此其所以海內富庶，錢朽粟紅。至於武帝之時，內侈土木，外勤兵役，海內虛耗，則財惡得而不匱哉？

賦役煩苛，隋不足道也。唐承隋後，授人以口分世業之田，加以太宗之敦行仁義，安養困窮，重民力而罷遠戍，鑒秦失而停𠠎村，此其所以斗米三錢，夜戶不閉。至於天
translation_en:
…to collect it, weighing the burdens and quantities, the locations within and without, and the distances near and far, and in every case establishing a balanced standard, without the slightest excess. This is what is meant by collecting wealth through righteousness. Furthermore, the nine standards of expenditure were established to govern its use. From sacrifices and the reception of guests to distributions of gifts and expenditures on goodwill offerings, all were apportioned and regulated accordingly. This is what is meant by using wealth according to ritual propriety. When these three principles are put into effect, the proper way of government is attained. As for Wang Mang’s earlier failure in applying them and Wang Anshi’s later failure, the fault lay not with the Rites of Zhou but with those who applied it. Confucius said: “If one wishes to put government into practice by following a model, the institutions of the Duke of Zhou remain.” Wang Tong likewise said: “If someone were to employ me, I would take this with me and proceed.” I have yet to see how one could properly discuss enduring institutions while setting aside the Offices of Zhou.

For burdensome taxation and labor service, Qin scarcely merits discussion. Taking warning from Qin’s abuses, Han levied a land tax of one-fifteenth. Moreover, Emperor Wen personally practiced frugality and devoted himself to allowing the people rest and recovery. He rejected fine horses rather than riding them and abandoned the proposed Dew Terrace rather than building it. This was why the realm became prosperous and populous, its stored coins decaying and its grain turning red with age. By Emperor Wu’s time, however, extravagant construction within and relentless military service abroad had depleted the realm. How could its wealth then fail to run short?

For vexatious and oppressive taxation and labor service, Sui scarcely merits discussion. Following Sui, Tang granted people individually allotted fields and hereditary holdings. Moreover, Emperor Taizong earnestly practiced benevolence and righteousness and provided security and sustenance for the destitute. Valuing the people’s labor, he abolished distant garrison service; taking warning from Qin’s failures, he halted “𠠎村” [?]. This was why a dou of rice cost three cash and doors were left unbolted at night. But by the time of Tian…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
寶之時內寵哲婦外縱強藩四方多事則
財惡得而不竭哉宋則版部有左計有右
計有總計其後三司有使度支有使磨勘
有司會計有錄祥符天禧之間可謂盛矣
然一壞於熈寧君臣之變更再壞於紹興
以後之妄費而用遂不可支矣恭惟
聖祖立國之初費用併集蠲租之令無歲不下
而財用不聞其有匱乏者蓋由
聖祖仁義之德本乎天性而儉約之風洽於海
===
內而又出納之有度也積貯之有素也然
而歷世既久用日以煩弊日以積其勢有
不得不然而矣惟我
皇上即位之初制節謹度宜夫財之無不足也
夫何頃年以來少有警急則動支內帑其
曷故哉蘇軾有曰爲國有三計九年之蓄
常閒而無用者萬世之計一歲之入纔足
以爲一歲之出者一時之計也至于最下
而無謀者量出以爲入用之不給則取之
punctuated:
寶之時，內寵哲婦，外縱強藩，四方多事，則財惡得而不竭哉？宋則版部有左計，有右計，有總計；其後三司有使，度支有使，磨勘有司，會計有錄。祥符、天禧之間，可謂盛矣。然一壞於熈寧君臣之變更，再壞於紹興以後之妄費，而用遂不可支矣。
恭惟聖祖立國之初，費用併集，蠲租之令無歲不下，而財用不聞其有匱乏者，蓋由聖祖仁義之德本乎天性，而儉約之風洽於海內，而又出納之有度也，積貯之有素也。然而歷世既久，用日以煩，弊日以積，其勢有不得不然而矣。惟我皇上即位之初，制節謹度，宜夫財之無不足也。夫何頃年以來，少有警急，則動支內帑，其曷故哉？
蘇軾有曰：「爲國有三計：九年之蓄，常閒而無用者，萬世之計；一歲之入，纔足以爲一歲之出者，一時之計也。至于最下而無謀者，量出以爲入，用之不給，則取之
translation_en:
…in the Tianbao era, he favored a meddling woman within the palace and gave powerful regional military governors free rein outside it. With troubles on every side, how could financial resources fail to be exhausted? Under the Song, the revenue administration [?] had offices for left accounts, right accounts, and consolidated accounts. Subsequently, the Three Fiscal Agencies had commissioners, the expenditure administration had commissioners, auditing had its responsible offices, and accounting had its records. During the Xiangfu and Tianxi eras, this could be called a flourishing system. Yet it was first damaged by the changes introduced by ruler and ministers during the Xining era, and damaged again by reckless expenditure from the Shaoxing era onward, until expenditure could no longer be sustained.
We reverently consider that, when the Sagely Founder first established the dynasty, expenses arose all at once, and not a year passed without an edict remitting land taxes; yet no shortage of funds was reported. This was because the Sagely Founder’s benevolence and righteousness were rooted in his innate nature, while his example of frugality spread throughout the realm. Moreover, receipts and disbursements were regulated, and reserves had been accumulated beforehand. Yet after many generations, expenditures grew daily more burdensome and abuses accumulated day by day: circumstances made this unavoidable [?]. When our present Emperor first ascended the throne, he imposed restraints and carefully observed proper limits; surely financial resources ought therefore to have been sufficient. Why, then, in recent years, has even a minor emergency prompted recourse to the Inner Treasury? What is the reason?
Su Shi once said: “There are three plans for governing a state. To maintain reserves sufficient for nine years, normally left idle and unused, is a plan for ten thousand generations. For one year’s revenue barely to suffice for one year’s expenditure is a plan for the moment. As for the lowest course, devoid of foresight: one determines revenue according to expenditure, and when funds do not suffice, one exacts from the people…”

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
益多此不終月之計也竊見夫入粟之令
數行而郡國之虛如故榷稅之官並設而
內帑之用不充萬世之計顧如是乎蘇軾
又曰足財之道非求財而益之也去其所
以害財而已害財有三吏冗一也兵冗二
也費冗三也竊見諸司有定員而武功之
賞太濫軍士多失伍而食粮之籍日增其
他不急之務無益之費亦往往有之則於
是三冗者夫亦未能免乎盖理財之道無
===
他在節與不節耳能節則雖虛必盈不節
則雖盈必虛節之為言人君制用之要誠
不踰此否則必為桑弘羊王安石之說非
國家所宜聞也洪惟我
皇上秉離照之明奮乾剛之斷務其所以生財
如周官之所載去其所以害財如蘇轍之
所謂惜名器而爵及有功慎錫予而賞以
天下然後可以議制用矣雖然非要也慎
乃儉德刑于家邦朴素之教始自貴近則
punctuated:
益多，此不終月之計也。竊見夫入粟之令數行，而郡國之虛如故；榷稅之官並設，而內帑之用不充。萬世之計，顧如是乎？蘇軾又曰：「足財之道，非求財而益之也，去其所以害財而已。害財有三：吏冗，一也；兵冗，二也；費冗，三也。」竊見諸司有定員，而武功之賞太濫；軍士多失伍，而食粮之籍日增；其他不急之務、無益之費，亦往往有之。則於是三冗者，夫亦未能免乎？盖理財之道無他，在節與不節耳。能節，則雖虛必盈；不節，則雖盈必虛。節之為言，人君制用之要，誠不踰此。否則必為桑弘羊、王安石之說，非國家所宜聞也。
洪惟我皇上，秉離照之明，奮乾剛之斷，務其所以生財，如《周官》之所載；去其所以害財，如蘇轍之所謂；惜名器而爵及有功，慎錫予而賞以天下，然後可以議制用矣。雖然，非要也。「慎乃儉德」，刑于家邦，朴素之教始自貴近，則
translation_en:
…ever more is exacted: this is a plan that cannot last even a month. I humbly observe that orders to contribute grain have repeatedly been issued, yet the prefectures remain as depleted as before; officials administering monopoly levies have been appointed, yet the funds of the imperial treasury remain insufficient. Can a plan for ten thousand generations really be like this? Su Shi further said: “The way to make revenues sufficient is not to seek wealth and increase it, but simply to eliminate what damages it. There are three things that damage wealth: superfluous officials, superfluous soldiers, and superfluous expenditure.” I humbly observe that, although the various offices have fixed staffing quotas, rewards for military merit are bestowed far too freely; many soldiers have left their units, yet the rolls of those drawing grain rations grow daily. Other nonessential undertakings and useless expenditures also occur frequently. Have we not, then, still failed to escape these three kinds of excess? The way to manage finances consists in nothing other than whether one exercises restraint. With restraint, even empty coffers will become full; without it, even full coffers will become empty. Restraint is truly the essential principle by which a ruler regulates expenditure; nothing goes beyond it. Otherwise, one inevitably adopts the doctrines of Sang Hongyang and Wang Anshi, which the state ought not to entertain.
I reverently reflect that Our Majesty possesses the illuminating clarity of Li, the trigram of fire, and exercises the firm decisiveness of Qian, the trigram of heaven. He should attend to the means of producing wealth, as recorded in the Offices of Zhou; eliminate what damages wealth, as Su Zhe described; cherish titles and insignia of rank, granting noble rank to those with merit; and exercise care in bestowing gifts, awarding rewards with the realm in view [?]. Only then can the regulation of expenditure be discussed. Yet even this is not the fundamental point. “Be mindful of your virtue of frugality”: set an example for the household and the state. If instruction in simplicity begins with the noble and those close to the throne, then…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
財用不期節而自節王制所謂十年之餘
蘇子所謂萬世之計庶幾在此矣謹對
punctuated: 財用不期節而自節，《王制》所謂十年之餘，蘇子所謂萬世之計，庶幾在此矣。謹對。
translation_en: …financial expenditure will become restrained of itself, without deliberate efforts to restrain it. The surplus sufficient for ten years spoken of in “Royal Regulations” (Wang zhi), and the plan for ten thousand generations spoken of by Master Su, may perhaps be realized through this. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
皇上嗣大歷服稽古圖治凡禮樂
刑政典章名物悉協厥中矧
取賢斂才之法尤
國家首務哉今年爲嘉靖戊子
秋八月寔維天下貢士之期
上命郎中臣日休主事臣龍主湖
===
廣試事臣等聞
命兢惕惟弗克祗承
明德識拔真才以弼
盛治是懼廼兼程而南就事事
竣當疏名梓文彙爲錄以
獻臣龍以職事謹拜手稽首序
其後臣惟文運之昌實與氣
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

皇上嗣大歷服，稽古圖治，凡禮樂刑政、典章名物，悉協厥中。矧取賢斂才之法，尤國家首務哉！今年爲嘉靖戊子，秋八月，寔維天下貢士之期。上命郎中臣日休、主事臣龍主湖廣試事。臣等聞命兢惕，惟弗克祗承明德、識拔真才以弼盛治是懼，廼兼程而南就事。事竣，當疏名梓文，彙爲錄以獻。臣龍以職事，謹拜手稽首，序其後。臣惟文運之昌，實與氣
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

His Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial mandate. He examines antiquity in seeking good government, ensuring that rites and music, punishments and administration, institutions and regulations, and the names and forms of things all accord with their proper mean. How much more, then, must the means of selecting worthy men and gathering talent be a foremost concern of the state!

This year, the wuzi year of Jiajing [1528], the eighth month in autumn was the appointed time for presenting scholars throughout the empire. His Majesty ordered your servants Rixiu, a Bureau Director, and Long, a Secretary, to preside over the Huguang examination. Upon receiving the command, we were apprehensive and vigilant, fearing only that we might fail reverently to uphold his luminous virtue and to recognize and select true talent to assist his flourishing rule. We therefore hastened south, covering successive stages without stopping, to undertake our duties. Once the work was completed, we were to list the names and print the writings from woodblocks, compiling them into a record for presentation to the throne. Your servant Long, in fulfillment of his official duties, reverently bows with hands joined and forehead to the ground and supplies this postface.

Your servant considers that the flourishing fortunes of literary culture are indeed interconnected with the vital forces…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
運相爲流通所以敦篤培養
斡旋轉移之機則在上之人
耳惟我
聖祖高皇帝繼天立極用夏變夷
以經術造天下之士雖諸子
史無不學而經爲重設科取
士雖論策諸文無不校而經
===
義爲主凡非聖之書不經之
學如近代詞章誦記之格悉
擯焉
列聖相承益隆紹述行之百六十
餘年于兹士爭自濯磨非六
經不以言非本諸身心該諸
物理不以學漸磨涵煦充足
punctuated:
運相爲流通，所以敦篤培養、斡旋轉移之機，則在上之人耳。惟我聖祖高皇帝繼天立極，用夏變夷，以經術造天下之士。雖諸子史無不學，而經爲重；設科取士，雖論策諸文無不校，而經義爲主。凡非聖之書、不經之學，如近代詞章誦記之格，悉擯焉。
列聖相承，益隆紹述，行之百六十餘年于兹。士爭自濯磨，非六經不以言，非本諸身心、該諸物理不以學。漸磨涵煦，充足
translation_en:
…the movement of vital force, with each circulating in concert with the other. The means of strengthening and nurturing them, and of directing and transforming them, lie solely with those above. Our sagely progenitor, the Exalted Emperor, succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, transforming the non-Chinese through Chinese civilization and forming the scholars of the realm through classical learning. Although they studied all the philosophical masters and histories, the classics held greatest weight. In establishing examinations to select scholars, although discourses, policy essays, and all other forms of writing were assessed, essays on the meaning of the classics were central. Writings that departed from the sages and learning that strayed from the classics, such as the recent practices of literary composition and rote memorization, were all excluded.
Successive sage emperors carried on this legacy, increasingly honoring and developing it. This system has now been practiced for more than 160 years. Scholars vie to purify and refine themselves. They will not speak except on the basis of the Six Classics, nor pursue learning unless it is rooted in their own persons and minds and encompasses the principles of things. Gradually polished and nurtured, they have attained a fullness…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有餘故凡形之啓沃紀之
國史布之祠祝著之章疏雖繁
簡華實不能盡同而
國初渾厚之氣淳朴之習皆於
是乎徵之恬熈既久文日益
盛而體裁之異不無漸失其
初者變而通之兹非其時乎
===
皇上頃緣大臣之議
特賜
明詔以風勵天下文體務在平實
爾雅根諸理覈諸事者進之
蓋將驅浮華詭異之習以復
我
祖宗渾厚淳古之風士際斯時亦
punctuated:
有餘，故凡形之啓沃，紀之國史，布之祠祝，著之章疏，雖繁簡華實不能盡同，而國初渾厚之氣、淳朴之習，皆於是乎徵之。恬熈既久，文日益盛，而體裁之異，不無漸失其初者。變而通之，兹非其時乎？

皇上頃緣大臣之議，特賜明詔，以風勵天下。文體務在平實爾雅，根諸理、覈諸事者進之。蓋將驅浮華詭異之習，以復我祖宗渾厚淳古之風。士際斯時，亦
translation_en:
…and more than sufficient. Thus, whenever this learning finds expression in counsel offered to the sovereign, is recorded in the dynastic history, is proclaimed in sacrificial prayers, or is set forth in memorials, although these writings cannot all be alike in length or in ornament and substance, the generous spirit and simple customs of the dynasty’s founding can be discerned in them all. After a long period of peace and prosperity, literary production has grown ever more abundant; yet, amid differences in form and style, some writings have gradually lost their original character. Is this not the time to make changes so that the tradition may continue to flourish?

His Majesty recently acted upon the deliberations of his high ministers and specially issued an illustrious edict to encourage and admonish all under Heaven. Literary style must be plain, substantial, refined, and correct; writings rooted in principle and verified against actual affairs are to be advanced. His purpose is to drive out habits of superficial ornament and eccentricity, restoring the generous, simple, and antique manner of our imperial ancestors. For scholars to live at such a time is also…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
何其幸哉宜必有光明俊偉
竒特之才穎脫其間者矣矧
兹荆湘之士涵濡
聖化尤深又安敢謂無若人褒然
為天下先者出邪孔子曰有
德者必有言顏淵曰舜何人
也予何人也有為者亦若是
===
夫文言之精者也兹多士見
錄有司馴且再升論定服有
官政尚舉所學與今日先資
之言力行以求其信本之於
身施之於民極之於輔理成
化舟楫霖雨若傅說之於高
宗篤棐迓衡若周公之於成
punctuated:
何其幸哉！宜必有光明俊偉、竒特之才穎脫其間者矣。矧兹荆湘之士涵濡聖化尤深，又安敢謂無若人褒然為天下先者出邪？孔子曰：「有德者必有言。」顏淵曰：「舜何人也？予何人也？有為者亦若是。」
夫文，言之精者也。兹多士見錄有司，馴且再升，論定，服有官政，尚舉所學與今日先資之言，力行以求其信。本之於身，施之於民，極之於輔理成化，舟楫霖雨若傅說之於高宗，篤棐迓衡若周公之於成
translation_en:
…how fortunate they are! Surely there must be men of brilliant, outstanding, and extraordinary talent who distinguish themselves among them. Moreover, the scholars of Jing and Xiang have been especially deeply imbued with the sage emperor’s transforming influence. How could one venture to say that no such men will emerge, conspicuously taking the lead throughout the realm? Confucius said: “Those who possess virtue must have words to express it.” Yan Yuan said: “What sort of man was Shun? What sort of man am I? Those who strive can likewise become such men.”
Literary composition is the refinement of speech. These many scholars have now been selected by the responsible officials. In due course they will advance through two further stages, be assessed and ranked, and undertake the duties of public office. May they put into vigorous practice what they have learned and the words that have served as their initial credentials today [?], seeking to substantiate them through action. Let them root this in their own persons, extend it to the people, and carry it to its fullest realization in assisting government and accomplishing moral transformation: serving as boat and oars, and as timely rain, as Fu Yue did for Gaozong; offering devoted assistance and securing peace, as the Duke of Zhou did for King Cheng…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
王世道亦或有攸賴以復古
者而何
國初人才之不相及哉則斯文
者雖謂之經緯天地固可也
祖宗之所深培厚植
皇上之所鼓舞作新均無負矣一
或工於詞而德之不孚言於
===
始而終之或違則藝焉而已
多士尚其思之毋使今日之
文後之人以藝觀之則至幸
焉臣玆濫竽校文之責極知
譾陋不足以仰副
皇上旁求之志然而惓惓以人事
君之誠亦自有不能已者故
punctuated:
王，世道亦或有攸賴以復古者，而何國初人才之不相及哉？則斯文者，雖謂之經緯天地，固可也。祖宗之所深培厚植，皇上之所鼓舞作新，均無負矣。一或工於詞而德之不孚，言於始而終之或違，則藝焉而已。多士尚其思之，毋使今日之文，後之人以藝觀之，則至幸焉。
臣玆濫竽校文之責，極知譾陋，不足以仰副皇上旁求之志。然而惓惓以人事君之誠，亦自有不能已者，故
translation_en:
…King Cheng, the course of the age might likewise find in them support for restoring antiquity. How, then, could they fail to match the men of talent of our dynasty’s founding years? Thus, it would indeed be fitting to call this literary and moral tradition the warp and weft of Heaven and Earth. Neither the deep cultivation and firm nurturing bestowed by the imperial ancestors nor His Majesty’s encouragement and renewal would then have been in vain. But if someone is skilled in phrasing yet lacks trustworthy virtue, or speaks at the outset but later departs from his words, his achievement is merely literary craft. You many scholars should reflect upon this. Do not let later generations regard today’s writings as mere literary craft: that would be the greatest blessing.
I, your servant, now unworthily bear responsibility for examining these writings. I know full well that my shallow learning is insufficient to fulfill His Majesty’s desire to seek worthy men far and wide. Yet my earnest sincerity in serving my ruler by finding men of worth is something I cannot suppress. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖七年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於錄之終以是告之
禮部祠祭清吏司主事吳龍
謹序
punctuated:
於錄之終，以是告之。
禮部祠祭清吏司主事吳龍謹序。
translation_en:
…at the end of this record, I offer these words to you.
Preface respectfully composed by Wu Long, Secretary in the Bureau of Sacrifices of the Ministry of Rites.
